text:
The refurbished Dell desktop itself is excellent. It arrived clean, runs smoothly, and performs exactly as advertised. For the price, it’s a great value.
The only real problem was the wireless adapter included in the box. It struggled to maintain a stable connection from the start, with frequent drops and inconsistent speeds. After a lot of frustration, I replaced it with a better-quality adapter, and the connectivity issues disappeared immediately. I contacted the seller’s AI‑assisted support system about Bluetooth connection to the motherboard, but the guidance wasn’t helpful. It repeatedly gave incorrect advice while insisting the issue was “almost resolved,” even though the root cause was simply not knowing the details about the motherboard. Due to a lack of F USB connection on the motherboard, the plug-in Bluetooth was never going to work.
Tip: Don’t plug in the included wireless adapter at all. It installs drivers that are difficult to remove and can interfere with other adapters. Upgrade your Wi‑Fi hardware first, and you’ll avoid a lot of unnecessary hassle.

Bottom line: The desktop is a great buy. Just skip the bundled wireless adapter and use your own from the start.

text: First of all, I am a fairly tech-savvy 72 year old and don't need a computer for work of any sort, but I use a desk top computer every day for news, email, banking, shopping, art tutorials and classes and a crossword or two. I also have a laptop (awesome Acer) that I use when I'm not in my art studio/office. So I don't need any super duper gaming computer, just basics. My expensive, 6 year old HP AIO Envy died on me and might have been fixable for a third time, but with all the shortages and price increases around the corner, I opted for a new one now while I can still get and afford it. Anyway, I chose this one. Not thrilled with it over all, but can't really say too much bad. Set up was extremely simple. The camera, however, is not real good for Zoom (at my age, though, no camera makes me look good) but I have a little plug in camera to use for that anyway, which is much better. All in all, I guess I like it enough, just not crazy in love with it like my Acer laptop.....maybe I should have bought another Acer???? title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I'd had a Lenovo AIO since early 2016 that was suffering under the twin strains of old age and constant Zoom meetings. There's a huge range of prices and features among available AIOs and much better screen/hard drive options than there was in '16. I wound up paying less than I had then while picking up the three things most important to me: a solid-state drive (to increase retrieval speed and eliminate machine noise during video conferences), the AMD Ryzen 5 processor, and lots of RAM. Another plus is the built-in DVD drive.

The new Lenovo is terrific: fast, quiet, and up to all of the general productivity, light graphics and data processing tasks I require. The touch screen is crisp and clear. The camera, located at the top center of the bezel, is not the best, but it's fine for 1080p and lower levels of resolution. Low-light photography is acceptable (in addition to video calls, I use this camera to record television press interviews; commercial stations have been satisfied with the quality). I also appreciate the physical lens blocker built into the housing of the computer.

I swapped the corded keyboard and mouse for cordless models -- a big reason to have an AIO is to reduce cable clutter -- but noted during setup that both were precise and the keyboard is clicky, a pleasure to type on. Packaging is minimal and operation couldn't be easier; I was up and running within minutes of taking the machine out of its box. The stand, a curved metal tube, it elegant and minimal. I've seen some users complain that the stand doesn't keep the screen straight: I've had no such problems.

All-in-all, I'm very satisfied with the computer, it's a terrific value.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
The Short Version: (Please skip this as it has spoilers if you prefer to read ‘The Long Version’.)
16 GB RAM, 1 TB M.2 SSD. I noticed a vibration from the CPU fan and contacted TekRefurbs and they are shipping me a new fan. Their response time was quick and they were eager to make sure I was a satisfied customer. I added 16 GB more RAM, a 2.5 inch SSD, a low-profile graphics card (supports up to 3 monitors), and a dual M.2 card along with 2 more M.2 SSDs. With the 2 DP ports and HDMI port on the motherboard, I ACTUALLY RAN 6 MONITORS (all at once) while streaming 6 different videos on YouTube. I picked this up to replace my DELL Optiplex 9020 which is too old for Windows 11. (As of now, Microsoft has stated that they will be ending their support for Win 10 by the end of 2024.) Running Crystal Disk Mark I got transfer rates of 1.7 GBps (read) and 1.1 GBps (write) on the SSD that came with the computer and 2 GBps (read) and 1.6 GBps (write) on the HP M.2 SSD I added. **UPDATE: I replaced one of my M.2 SSDs with a fanxiang S660 4TB PCIe 4.0 NVMe M.2 SSD and now get the following speeds (read) 3.5 GBps and (write) 3.1 GBps. They actually make faster M.2s but they far exceed the capability of the motherboard.

I’m thrilled with both the computer and customer service couldn’t be happier with this purchase.

The Long Version:
I have purchased over 1,000 items from Amazon over the past decade and I only give reviews on the best (or the worst) items I have ordered. The renewed DELL Optiplex 7060 SFF I got from TekRefurbs is amazing and so is their customer support. (I had a little vibration with the CPU fan and I sent them a message about it, they replied the next business day and offered to send a replacement.) Awesome service!

With Microsoft stating that they will be ending their support for Windows 10 towards the end of 2024, I decided to replace my Optiplex 9020 SFF (not Win 11 compatible) now, rather than wait for a possible shortage of affordable/renewed Win 11 computers in the future. (As of now, the vast majority of people are still running Win 10.)

The model that I got was the 16 GB/ 1 TB version (other variants may be sold by different vendors). When I opened the box (and even the case) it looked like it was brand new, I couldn’t find even the smallest amount of dust anywhere. Included with the desktop was a free wireless mouse & keyboard and a few BT & WiFi dongles in addition to the built-in features from the motherboard itself. (Even without the dongles, I still have BT & WiFi connectivity.) **Models sold by TekRefurbs come with the built-in M.2 WiFi card which supports both 5 & 2.4 Ghz but for the fun of it I replaced it with the AX210 WiFi 6E Card M.2 NGFF and connected it to the 2 internal antennas.

Display Support: While some desktops (from other sellers) only have 2 Display Ports (DP) and either a VGA port (or missing the 3rd port), mine came with 2 DPs and an HDMI port. (Nice touch!) While being able to connect to 3 monitors (off of the motherboard) is nice, I added an inexpensive VisionTek Products Radeon 6350 SFF 1GB DDR3 3M DMS59 with 2X DVI-I to VGA Adapter Graphics Card that adds support for an additional 3 monitors AND I RAN A TOTAL OF 6 MONITORS AT ONCE while streaming different videos on each monitor. Granted, I’m not a gamer so I’m not concerned with Frames Per Second (FPS) but it did actually work (I normally just run 3 monitors stacked vertically – one on top of each other).

Storage Capacity (hard drives): This model, like most of the DELL SFF cases have 3 SATA ports and the newer models have a space for an M.2 SSD. The model I purchased came with a 1 GB M.2 SSD and the DVD drive and the cables were provided to connect a second hard drive as well. There is room for a 3.5 inch hard drive or you can get an adapter to mount the smaller 2.5 inch drive if you wish (there are adapters that can hold up to three 2.5 inch drives in a single 3.5 inch slot). But why settle for just one additional hard drive when you can have a total of FOUR HARD DRIVES? Thanks to the Dual M.2 PCIE Adapter for SATA or PCIE NVMe SSD with Advanced Heat Sink Solution,M.2 SSD NVME (m Key) and SATA (b Key) 22110 2280 2260 2242 2230 to PCI-e x 4 Host Controller Expansion Card, you can have up to 3 M.2 SSDs plus one 2.5 inch SSD. ***You can also get the M.2 NVME to PCIe 3.0 x4 Adapter with Aluminum Heatsink Solution (single M.2 slot) and add up to two additional 2.5 inch SSDs. I actually recommend getting this card instead of the one I purchased because the second M.2 slot has to connect to one of the SATA ports from the motherboard so the transfer speed is the same as if you connected a 2.5 inch SSD (which are cheaper). Running Crystal Disk Mark I got transfer rates of 1.7 GBps (read) and 1.1 GBps (write) on the M.2 SSD that came with the computer and 2 GBps (read) and 1.6 GBps (write) on the HP M.2 SSD I added.

RAM: The model I purchased came with 16 GB RAM (two 8 GB chips) which was nice because I added an additional 16 GB RAM for a small price. (32 GB is more than enough RAM for most applications.)

Free Extras: The extra dongles, mouse and keyboard are nice touches and pretty good quality as well. I admit that I haven’t tested them because I used a lighted keyboard (wired) and Logitech Trackball.

Summary: Whether you are using the computer ‘as is’ or you want to upgrade it, this is an excellent choice for an affordable and (still) powerful system that will carry you through the Windows 11 lifespan (and probably beyond). Despite this being the Small Form Factor (SFF) model, there is room to add a (low profile) graphics card, USB-C 3.2 card, M.2 card or whatever you wish. (Just be mindful of the power requirements of the graphics cards - this comes with a 200 watt power supply.)

UPDATE 2/25/26:

This is still a great deal for the money. It has worked flawlessly. I'm adding a star because of the seller's behavior. RenewByte-Quality Recertified helped me quickly, efficiently and without hassling me about the problem I encountered and the solution.

I needed to implement NFS services on this system. I intentionally bought something running Pro because I anticipated this being a need. I went to activate the feature, and it wasn't there. I dug around and found that Win 11 Home had actually been installed. To me, this was a no brainer, easy think to fix knowing how the refurb market works, and it's an easy mistake to make, so shouldn't be any sweat. It took me longer working with Amazon to get a solid answer as to who specifically sold this to me through the Amazon refurb store than it did for RenewByte to solve my problem. All you need in this case is the right Product key and you can upgrade Home to Pro in-place (in case you didn't know that).

RenewByte was ON IT. As soon as I figured out it was them (and not the three other places Amazon pointed me at) they listened to the problem, understood the problem as I articulated it, and got me the right product key, which, of course, worked. My wife's system now has Win 11 Pro, not Home and all it took was a reboot to complete the process once I put the key in.

They could have, and I indeed have had other refurb groups run me around the mulberry bush to do a return because that's somehow "easier" for them when the only problem is something small like a card failed that I could replace on my own. RenewByte didn't do that. They took care of me with the least amount of friction possible.

THANK YOU, RenewByte, I will be looking to you for my future needs in this class of machine without looking at others, based on your customer service.

************************

This is a great deal for a productivity system. The unit is fast, and if you've got your MS account tied to your Windows machine, it really is an easy process to migrate systems, even from Win 10. As someone who has a heightened sense of security and data privacy I'm not a huge fan of that, but it does work super smooth.

For conducting online meetings with Teams or Zoom, MS Office work with large Word docs or Excel spreadsheets, it just cranks. The network is fast, it has plenty of USB ports and is not loud. I don't use the WiFi but it works and is decently fast. One thing I like about these Dell SFF systems is they are still expandable. There are 2 PCIe slots available, a bank of memory slots open, and I slapped a second SATA SSD for some working scratch space into the unit with zero issues.

I would imagine based on how well it performs that it could be used as a kids gaming machine. It would run Minecraft without breaking a sweat for sure, but for serious gamers you'd want something with more video capability.

I have used another one of these (though a 5070) as a linux jump server, and it works really well for that as well. It's tough to beat the price for what this system provides.

Great machine, but two cons that might leave some people stuck and disappointed.
First the potential biggy. The system came with NO power cord. Oops!
Also, as other another review stated, the Wi-Fi is NOT built in by DELL as the description states. It is a tiny $5 USB type
but it works just fine and this makes no difference to me, but it might to some.
FYI, if you get this machine and the Wi-Fi sees access points but will not connect, try a different USB port. I started with the 4th USB3 (blue) port on the right and no go. I moved it to the first on the left, and it has been solid now for a few days. I don't know why this would happen, but I got it working so no big deal.
Neither of those issues flustered me, your mileage may vary.
I got this refurb PC because of its 8 core i7-9700, 32GB RAM and 1TB SDD all for a great price.
If you have never owned one of these DELL commercial grade machines, you will not be disappointed. The build quality and the heavy sheet metal used in these units is far superior to a discount consumer grade PC. I have had four similar mini towers like this over the years - 2 HP and 2 DELL, but this is the most powerful one yet. The $400 price point makes it a no-brainer for most business and home office uses. It runs Win11, Libre Office, some trading and charting platforms, and FL Studio DAW all at the same time without hesitation. The 32GB RAM no doubt helps with that.
The unit arrived well packed for shipping and reasonably clean, though it had what I thought at first was a small scratch on top. This turned out to be a splash of white-out from its past corporate life.
As I mentioned above, what could be a showstopper for most users looking for a turnkey machine, this unit arrived with no power cord. Now, having been a PC hardware nerd for decades, I have dozens of the standard power cords laying around, and it did not slow me down a bit. Obviously, though, a power cord should come in the box, and most likely will in yours. I can't imagine they left it out on purpose.
I have not tested the included CHEAP wireless keyboard and mouse, but I am sure they are fine for what they are and are probably an upgrade for laptop keyboard users.
Great value, in a small, solid package.

text: I am using this for a basic email and web surfer machine. It is very fast..... looks and runs like a brand new machine. Came with a new keyboard and mouse (not refurb) but the most basic cheap KB and mouse. The machine specs out exactly as advertised. Even came with CD/DVD player/ burner. The case is small form factor, so do not get it with the expectation of getting and doing a lot of upgrades. There is a PCI Express. There were NO unpleasant or unexpected surprises. Runs super quiet.... really not bad at all. Here is the deal as to why its so cheap for the most part. The copy of windows is an OEM version issued and licensed exclusively to Dell. You do not get a copy of Windows on disc with this machine, you get a hard drive with an image file on it ( the main drive has a partition on it) which is where the copy is located. You can do full factory restore from that partition and set the machine up like it was the day you got it and it will activate and be a legitimate copy/machine.... BUT it only works on the machine it shipped out with (or one just like it) Microsoft has almost reached the end of life with Win 10.... set for about Oct 2025. I ran the test to see if the machine would take win 11 upgrade and it says NO...however a Google search results many people saying they have run it just fine. The primary reason it fails is the processor. It is not in the recommended list of processors that Microsoft recommends for Windows 11. It passed on every thing else. And like I said there have been many folks who have said they have installed it (win 11) and it is running just fine with this very processor. In conclusion at this price it is almost basically a disposable cup...wait I mean PC, LOL.... you could just buy a new one every couple of years. Or you can do as I am going to and get the latest copy of Linux / Ubuntu Wilma and run that. (free for personal use) You can burn a copy that will boot and run from a USB drive if you want to try before installing (I have no affiliation with Linux or make any thing off this suggestion, its just something I personally like) Ok to end this, I have worked on/built computers for the last 30 + years and have quite a large knowledge base and I just can not find any reason to complain about this PC/purchase.

I bought this for my girlfriend as her first computer 4 days ago (12-01-25) and today (12-05-25) the power supply literally blew up. It made a super loud pop sound and immediately shut off without warning. Upon opening it up, a white chalky looking thing came out which is typically from a capacitor. I thought at first it may have been the motherboard, but apon looking, it was fine. I took the power supply out of the pc and visually inspected it and seen nothing wrong.

I jumped the power and ground on the power supply, nothing happened. No fan or anything. So I checked with a multimeter and got 0 volts from any wire. The grounds were fine since they had 0hms.

I am a bit tech savvy so I will not be returning or sending in for warranty. I have since ordered a replacement power supply. I did not feel like packaging up everything for someone 35 dollar upgrade. It came with a 225 watt power supply and ordered a 255.

If you dont know what you're doing with computers, I suggest you get a brand new computer. Not a refurbished one. I took a chance knowing something may happened due to the seemingly never ending stream of similar instances in the reviews.

It does have rgb which is okay, it ran pretty smoothly and did run the sims on medium low graphics, the wifi adapter is pretty okay, it was doing 100+ mbps and 50+ upload. However, none of that makes it worth even 2 stars considering we've had it for 4 days.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
Two things to note, I don't often review products, and I specifically selected STG as the reseller given their positive reviews over the last 12 months, even though I paid $2.00 more and also had to wait an extra day or two for their shipping, it was well worth it.

Not to sound harsh but we as consumers should take some responsibility of what we are purchasing are also specifically who is the reseller, especially when you are buying a refurbished item. You are generally always presented with the cheapest purchase option, that doesn’t mean it is your best option, especially when it comes to refurbished items like PC’s. Keep in mind, this is not a brand-new sparkly PC with a $2K price tag, in the best-case scenario, you are buying a 5-year-old PC, that hopefully was sitting on some drones desk in nice clean office environment, which has now depreciated and is being re-sold back into the mainstream consumer market. The most important part of this process is the cleaning up, reconfiguring and packaging of the PC from its previous life to now being in your most likely, home environment.

STG did a great job of this, the PC was dust free inside, was in pristine condition and from what I can tell, they even put in a new battery on the motherboard (this is to keep the bios going when unplugged, it’s a small battery most people don’t even know exist). It was well packaged, included a very easy to follow single page guide to get Windows activated with Microsoft and they even included a keyboard and mouse for folks who might need it to get started. I will note that the PC itself only has 3 - Display Ports, I missed that in the description but that is on me, not an issue for most people so I just added an HDMI dongle. On a side note, yes, it does have plenty of USB ports, on the front and back, but also has the old school PS/2 style ports available for a mouse and keyboard for nostalgia's sake...ironically, I still have an old trackball mouse that would work on this thing lol.

After getting Windows activated, I immediately added a 2TB NVME drive for the boot drive and cloned the original 1TB SSD through Acronis, which is free to use if you use a Western Digital drive. I then added a dual port 10GB SFP+ network card, an additional 3.5” SATA drive for more storage which I had sitting around, and then added two 16GB DDR4 RAM sticks to get it up to a total of 64GB of RAM. I could not find the exact ADATA ones that came with it, but I did match up the RAM’s speed, voltage and timings to make sure it would work, and it did. Also, I did update the BIOS and some other items from Dell’s website but most people will never need to do this, and in all honesty shouldn’t. I would recommend the RAM I bought but I honestly don't know if it is the same as what came in yours and it may do more harm than good.

This is the first PC I have purchased in about 30 years, I have been building my own since I was a kid in the 90’s but I really just needed a decent PC I could RDP into, use as a management device for my network rack, and also serve as a VM host device using VirtualBox with an Ubuntu and Linux Mint VM. I know Dell is pretty solid when it comes to desktops like these, which are usually targeted at businesses, so my hope is that it just sits in my basement next to the network rack for another 5 years, if it is still running after that, it will just become a full blown linux box.

This is a great little PC as is, but with a few upgrades can be a utility device like what I did, or a light little gaming rig assuming you upgrade the PSU or get a GPU that doesn't need a lot of space or power. Just understand, this is never going to be something you overclock or turn into a 4K 120fps gaming rig, it just doesn't have the space or backbone for it, nor was it ever intended to. It draws very little power, has a nice quiet case and does have WiFi and BT built in if you need it.

Once again, I cannot say enough good things about STG, they did a great job and I would have no problems buying from them again. It was nice to see a seller actually take pride in what they sent, as always, it was the little things that made a big difference for the user/consumer experience!

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
First some background:
I am not a Dell lover, more of a Dell Hater. I don't like how they used specialized components in their computers. This one is no different, use this as is, it can't really be upgraded. Power supply is a dell custom one, and it's tiny. Having said that, this one has turned out to be a really nice computer.
Cosmetic:
This computer visually has no issues, no scratches and the inside had zero dust in it.
Components:
The components are about 3 to 5 years old according to the counters on the hard drives. One of the drives is an M.2 Samsung drive made specifically for Dell, it contains the OS (I call these gumsticks because of their shape). The second drive is a 2.5 inch 1TB drive. It's empty. This computer allows for toolless installation of hard drives, which is great. I replaced the 2.5 1TB drive with a 3.5 8TB drive with zero issue. There is only one SATA power and data cable spot on the motherboard, so it can't fit more than 1 hard drive along with the gumstick. It comes with a keyboard and mouse. I didn't use them, so I can't comment. It also has bluetooth I guess. I use a hardwired ethernet connection so i can't speak to any wireless connections.
Initialization:
During initialization I logged into my Microsoft account and everything worked flawlessly. I didn't have to enter an activation code like the STG Skytech Global paperwork said I would have to. I later went on my Microsoft account and verified this computer was registered with Windows 11 pro. I don't know anything about STG, but this computer was well cleaned and setup, so good for them. I left the computer on and occasionally cycled power over a full day to get all the windows 11 updates before I tried to do anything to the computer. I would recommend this to everyone. Let windows get fully updated before continuing. I'm not at Windows version 25H2. No issues. No display glitches that some people have indicated. Again, I would recommend not altering the computer for a day, until windows has updated to 25H2. I keep doing the 'check for updates' in windows to make this go faster.
Performance:
This computer takes about 15 seconds to boot. Very fast. Draws about 30 watts even when performing a disk transfer of 3TBs. I have no idea how they get the power so low. I haven't played games on it, nor would I suggest it. I'm using this as a backup system for my main computer. There is no external video card.
Conclusion:
I really am impressed with this computer. It's very small, uses almost no power, and allows me to connect via my local network to my main computer for backing up files. And it has windows 11 pro installed.

I ordered up 14 of these units (a couple different orders) and started installing them in client locations. Within a week, we started getting calls about the units trying to boot from PXE or saying "Operating System not found." Thought it was a fluke at first but eventually determined that this company has their own white-labeled M.2/PCIe SSDs and this series of Optiplex 7010s do NOT like them. In the end, we ended up having to replace the half dozen or so units we couldn't really swap out with new, brand-name SSDs to resolve the problem.

We did manage to return 7 of them, but I had to go buy big boxes as we'd already tossed the ones they were delivered in. Then we had to hound Amazon for several days to get the seller to actually refund the money (several days in, two of them had been refunded, but Amazon's site just kept saying "Refund in process" and they'd refund the money once they all were received). After a few pokes at Amazon, we did get our money back, but man did this cost me a lot of man hours having to rebuild failed/incompatible SSDs on the fly.

I don't know what's wrong with their white-labeled SSDs, but they must be incredibly cheap (and modern Optiplex units only really like NVMe models that can run in native RAID mode).

For the record, I did go to their web site and it looks like it was done in Microsoft Word. I managed to get a request out explaining my situation but only got a "please create a ticket" response.

I'd used OEMGENUINE in the past with good results, but wow was this a disaster. Do NOT buy these units unless you intend to put a quality SSD in it!!

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
First some background:
I am not a Dell lover, more of a Dell Hater. I don't like how they used specialized components in their computers. This one is no different, use this as is, it can't really be upgraded. Power supply is a dell custom one, and it's tiny. Having said that, this one has turned out to be a really nice computer.
Cosmetic:
This computer visually has no issues, no scratches and the inside had zero dust in it.
Components:
The components are about 3 to 5 years old according to the counters on the hard drives. One of the drives is an M.2 Samsung drive made specifically for Dell, it contains the OS (I call these gumsticks because of their shape). The second drive is a 2.5 inch 1TB drive. It's empty. This computer allows for toolless installation of hard drives, which is great. I replaced the 2.5 1TB drive with a 3.5 8TB drive with zero issue. There is only one SATA power and data cable spot on the motherboard, so it can't fit more than 1 hard drive along with the gumstick. It comes with a keyboard and mouse. I didn't use them, so I can't comment. It also has bluetooth I guess. I use a hardwired ethernet connection so i can't speak to any wireless connections.
Initialization:
During initialization I logged into my Microsoft account and everything worked flawlessly. I didn't have to enter an activation code like the STG Skytech Global paperwork said I would have to. I later went on my Microsoft account and verified this computer was registered with Windows 11 pro. I don't know anything about STG, but this computer was well cleaned and setup, so good for them. I left the computer on and occasionally cycled power over a full day to get all the windows 11 updates before I tried to do anything to the computer. I would recommend this to everyone. Let windows get fully updated before continuing. I'm not at Windows version 25H2. No issues. No display glitches that some people have indicated. Again, I would recommend not altering the computer for a day, until windows has updated to 25H2. I keep doing the 'check for updates' in windows to make this go faster.
Performance:
This computer takes about 15 seconds to boot. Very fast. Draws about 30 watts even when performing a disk transfer of 3TBs. I have no idea how they get the power so low. I haven't played games on it, nor would I suggest it. I'm using this as a backup system for my main computer. There is no external video card.
Conclusion:
I really am impressed with this computer. It's very small, uses almost no power, and allows me to connect via my local network to my main computer for backing up files. And it has windows 11 pro installed.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
If this PC matches your needs, it is an excellent buy.
Comments:
It has two expansion slots, one short, one full. Both PCIe. (The current picture shows four expansion slots. This is an error, it has two.)
It has room for two SATA SSDs (it comes with one, 1TB SSD.). I read somewhere that the max size is 2 TB, so the max internal storage would be 4 TB. If you add a second drive, you'll need a SATA data cable and a SATA power splitter (1 to 2) and a mounting bracket (The bay is for a 3.5" drive, most SATA drives are 2.5".)

The literature says it comes with five USB-3 and four USB-2 ports. All 9 ports are colored black. Normally USB-3 is colored blue. Based on the exposed pins inside of the ports, the four in front are USB-2, and the 5 in back are USB-3.1 (AFAICT.) USB 3.1 gen 1 supports transfer speeds of up to 5 Gbps. USB 3.1 gen 2 supports transfer speeds of up to 10 Gbps. As I read the spec I think it has gen 1 (5 Gbps.)

It comes with two display ports. If your monitor only has HDMI inputs, you will need an adapter. It also has VGA output.

I got the 32 GB memory version -- it is very fast. I would recommend also getting the insurance for any renewed item.

If you need more storage, use a USB drive. If you want it fast, use USB 3.2 gen 2x2 (20 Gbps.) You can also get a larger capacity drive (~20TB). For Gen 3.2 2x2 you'll need to use the short expansion slot for a USB 3.2 gen 2x2 card. Use the Small Form Factor (SFF) size. Usually a SFF USB card supports 2 drives.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
What I needed:
I needed a computer for my electronics lab. It didn't need to be immensely powerful, but I wanted something that would be easy to expand as needed. This PC met my needs almost perfectly, and at a very economical price. I purchased this 6 months ago (almost to the day), so this is not an "out of the box" impression, but one based on months of experience. It has been powered on (or sleeping) continuously, so I can remote access it when needed.

My uses are primarily centered around my lab work: Electronic Design, PCB Layout, and 3D Rendering of PCBs, along with Design of small enclosures and modest software development. I also have several PC connected pieces of bench equipment: Digital Scope, Power Supplies, Function Generator, and whatever thing I'm creating. Most of these connect via USB, and one via RS-232.

This PC:
You can see in the pictures that the front panel has 4 USB ports - 2 are SuperSpeed. These have already proven valuable for quick attachments.

The rear panel is loaded up with 6 more USB ports (2 of which are SuperSpeed), and I've used most of them. If I had to, I could easily dig out an old PS2 Keyboard to free up another USB port - but with 4 empty ports on the front I'm ok for now.

As noted above, I needed RS-232, and this PC had one - which is a bonus. Of course, I could have plugged in a USB to RS-232 adapter. Beneath the back-panel RS-232 port (the gray plug in the picture) is a VGA connector, which I don't expect to use. To the left of those are a couple of Display Ports - one connected to my big screen (3440 x 1440). The specs say that each can support a 4K monitor, but my bench doesn't have space (and the screen resolution works for my eyeballs and needs).

The host processor in the unit I purchased is an i5-4590 quad core running at 3.3 GHz. The motherboard memory slots are full, loaded with 16 GB of RAM. The motherboard has 3 SATA ports, but they are fully occupied, connected to a 240 GB SSD hosting Win10 Pro, a 1GB spinning HDD, and a DVD drive. The graphics is served with an integrated Intel HD 4600. For further expansion, there are 4 PCIe slots: 2 x X1, 1 x X4 and 1 x X16.

Other Discoveries:
* The BIOS still had the name of the prior "owner" (a company), which is probably where many of these came from. It was simple to change, so now is hosts a name appropriate for my lab.
* This PC is not for gaming, so I didn't rate that since I've never run a game on it. With my single high-resolution monitor connected, spinning a 3D model of a modestly complex circuit board is fast - it more than meets my needs.
* And I had no need for Tech Support, so I didn't rate that either.

My Expansion:
* In the pictures you'll see one of the PCI slots is occupied - with the 4-channel SATA adapter that I added. The 3 on the motherboard were occupied but I needed one more for an external HD dock.
* I expect to add a Webcam soon.
* I also expect to add one more PCI card to it, to add USB-C connectors. My newest gear (Laptop, Phone, etc.) all have USB-C, so this will be necessary.

My Summary:
This was the right PC for my needs. It was also relatively inexpensive. It has been running close to non-stop since my unboxing. It "seems" quiet enough for most any location, but my lab isn't the best place to judge that.

It didn't have support for every interface I needed but was more than expandable enough to add to it. I do wish the overall unit was a bit smaller (for my lab space), and in years prior I had a large tower PC, but tired of crawling under the desk to swap cables around.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
It was delivered on time and was in like-new condition as advertised. It has a smaller footprint than a full-size desktop which I had concerns about before I got it. However, once I opened the access panel, I was impressed. It has a recessed latched pull handle that removes the whole access panel exposing everything and no screws to unscrew or lose. Inside, not a speck of dust, literally, like a new computer, you can't tell that it's renewed/upgraded.

Even though it's smaller everything is easy to see and get to so if you need or want to do anything inside it's awesome. You can see everything and get to it with ease. You don't have to be a contortionist or have tiny hands and fingers. The drives and optical reader (DVD) are contained within a rack that you just pivot upward to release and you have full easy access to them. Additional expansion slots to add what you like. If you should want to increase RAM from 16 to 32 GB there is nothing around them so removing and replacing them in the slots would be effortless. I was surprised how cool this computer runs even when using multiple high resource software at the same time with no lag.

As for the USB Keyboard and Mouse, USB WiFi Adapter. These are low cost and just so you have something. As low cost as keyboard and mouse are I really like them. If you use something else don't throw them out as others have said. Save them as an emergency back up or give them to someone. I have a Logitech wireless keyboard and mouse but still using the ones that came with this computer. USB WiFi Adapter isn't the best it's not real fast and not great for long-distance so I did buy a better one at the same time. There are a lot of cheap USB WiFi Adapters that stop working after 2-3 months but here is a low-cost $17 good one I use so can avoid the hassle.
Just search amazon for -
TP-Link AC600 USB WiFi Adapter for PC (Archer T2U Plus)- Wireless Network Adapter for Desktop with 2.4GHz, 5GHz High Gain Dual Band 5dBi Antenna, Supports Windows 10/8.1/8/7/XP, Mac OS 10.9-10.14
It increased my transfer speed from 300 Mbps or less and 3 bars signal strength to a transfer speed of 433 to 490 Mbps and 5 bars signal strength.

All you have to do is connect a monitor, the keyboard, mouse, and USB wifi adapter and power up. You do need to set up you user account like any new computer. This is Microsoft so it wants you to use a Microsoft account to have a better "online experience". But all you need to do is enter your login for a Microsoft email account or create one during set up. That step requires connecting to the internet and entering the password. Or you can create an offline user account like the old days. The rest of the setup questions are about your preferences and you're ready to go.

Windows 10 Pro works perfectly. My daughter got one of these a while ago and wouldn't stop praising it so I got one. She gave me a heads up about the USB WiFi Adapter solution too. I couldn't be happier with this purchase.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
Background: We are blessed in our family to have someone who knows a lot about PCs, so we’re not overly intimidated by needing to replace things inside a PC or trouble shooting. Some of the other purchaser’s negative reviews on this machine were daunting to me though, but the price was so good for the specs, we decided to try it in spite of some of the bad reviews. We concurrently use PCs and Macs of varying ages and operating systems. This is the 2d refurbished machine we’ve ever purchased (the other refurbished PC was a $100 refurbished HP years ago from Overstock.com that’s still working great), but from the varying experiences reflected in the reviews, it may be a bit of a roll of the dice. I like that Amazon is behind this product.

Experience so far: It’s been almost two months of DAILY HEAVY USE on this PC, even creating 3D graphics using Blender, and so far this PC is working great. Very fast efficient start up. Tackles memory hog tasks such as 3D rendering with Blender software well (especially for the price of the PC). However it’s relatively early days, so I still have some doubts of longevity (mostly because of the other Amazon reviews).
So for what it’s worth, here’s my experience so far (from the reviews it appears there’s quite a bit of difference from person to person so read others reviews too). I’m writing the good and bad.
1) The PC arrived NOT well packaged for shipping, so I was dubious it wasn’t damaged. I felt the packing was so bad it disrespected the customer’s time because it seemed so likely the PC would be damaged simply because of poor packaging. For example, the exterior shipping box was damaged and the there was way too much room inside the shipping box for the PC tower to slip around. Luckily, somehow our PC survived the shipping, but the seller should fix this easy fix. Dear Seller: Please pack the PCs as if you had to use the PC yourself. Why go through all that work in refurbishing only to risk screwing it up in the shipping? -so even though the PC actually did work (hurray!), it worked in spite of the sloppy packaging, so I’d rate the packaging as needlessly carelessly bad. It also made me hope the restoration was done with more care and pride in workmanship than the packing was. Not a confidence/goodwill builder, sadly.
2). The PC arrived with a very basic keyboard that is 100% perfect for my needs (I use four computers side-by-side, so keyboard space is at a premium, so I actually love the keyboard, nice large clear letters on each key, easy to read and yet still efficiently space saving).
3) The PC arrived with a basic mouse, a bit smaller-sized but works 100% fine.
4) The PC itself looks as it should, except the seller put a BIG ugly white service sticker on top of the PC in a prominent place, not at all attractive, so I hope the seller reads this and uses more discreet sticker placement for other buyers. The ugly large white service sticker essentially kills any aesthetic/freshness the PC Tower could have.
5) The PC came with a small white wireless dongle that if you want wireless will take up one of the USB ports.
6) With great intrepidation, fearing the worst due to the poor shipping packaging, I hooked up the PC to its mouse and keyboard (and one of my monitors) and turned on the PC. EVERYTHING worked fine. The wireless dongle worked. It booted up. It was super SUPER fast. Eventually we used Ethernet cable instead of wireless Wi-Fi, and the Ethernet connection works fine too. I’ve used the PC to read CDs/DVDs and burned a test DVD just to make sure it works. It does. At least so far :)
7) Because this PC is NOT upgradable to Win 11, etc., be realistic. AFTER I felt the PC was working by running it through its paces, that’s when I bought software for it. In other words, given the negative reviews, make sure you like what you get before investing in software, BUT BEFORE YOU BUY RESEARCH THE AVAILABILITY OF THE SOFTWARE YOU USE FOR WINDOWS 10 Pro. Once you’ve run the PC through its paces, that’s when I recommend you actually buy the most recent version of the software you use that is compatible with Windows 10pro, because eventually the software companies won’t be supporting Windows 10 anymore. (By way of example, the last version of Adobe Photoshop that you could buy to own (as opposed to rent monthly) is not compatible with operating systems past Windows 7, so for the rest of my life I’ll need a Windows 7 machine to use that older Adobe software; similarly if you don’t want to pay a monthly subscription fee for Word/Excel/etc., you’ll need to buy a version of Office that is still compatible with Windows 10 pro (I bought Office 2019 Pro).
8) So this PC has worked well for me with Blender, Outlook, Excel, Word, and the operating system/computer surprisingly came pre-loaded with various software things - even an interesting 3D program (that was a happy surprise, must be part of Windows 10 pro!?!), and I’ve used the PC for the internet, and the PC networked easily to the printer, etc.
9) Eventually all PCs die/fritz. I backup at least daily to an external hard drive, because you just never know (and this is a refurbished PC, especially given the reviews, be realistic and backup backup backup.
Bottom line: This is a speedy effective PC that so far is doing what I need it to do at a great price. There are some super easy fixes the seller can do (BETTER PACKAGING FOR SHIPPING & PLACE THE SERVICE STICKER IN A LESS VISIBLE PLACE). I didn’t need to contact the seller for anything because this PC booted up easily. If everyone had my experience I’d say buy without hesitation; I wonder how many of the bad experiences could have been avoided by better packaging? In any event, so far my experience is FANTASTIC FOR THE PRICE :)
6-17-22 update: it’s still working GREAT, super fast, this morning I thought to myself what an excellent purchase this has been so far. Still FANTASTIC FOR THE PRICE. title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I purchased "renewed" or refurbished computer from and Amazon affiliated company in the past and it worked perfectly. So I was confident about purchasing a second "renewed" computer. I am a professional Hollywood recording engineer and music video director/producer. In my business, speed is critical. I need at least 32 GB RAM. Having a 1 TB hard drive is also helpful with the professional programs that I utilized (Avid Protools, Waves, SoundToys, FabFilter, etc.)

This new computer arrived well packed (box with foam, within another box). Everything works perfectly. System checks confirm: 32 GB RAM, IntelCore i7 processer, 1 TB hard drive. Windows 10 was already installed, and it was like I bought it new (company obtains official permission to reissue Windows 10). A dongle is included for Wi-Fi (don't let that bother you, it is small, goes in the back, and is no big deal). The dongle was plug-n-play and found my Wi-Fi without any problems. After I entered my Wi-Fi password, the computer set up just fine. I was able to install my Wi-Fi printer without any problem. The computer has 10 USB ports, of which I believe 4 are USB 3.

After Windows personalized set up, I proceeded to download Adobe Premier, Photoshop, After-Effects, and Illustrator without any problems.

I purchased a 27-inch curved Dell monitor which accepts the DisplayPort cable that this high quality Dell computer uses. (You can buy converters to go from DisplayPort to HDMI if you monitor does not have a DisplayPort input - which works just fine - I did that with my prior "renewed" Dell computer). Get gold-tipped ones for better signal transmission.

For the CPU speed, 32 GB RAM, and 1 TB hard drive, I saved myself about $2000 - $3000 in today's marker (April 2021). For those of you who have home recording studios, you will never match the speed of a desktop computer for the price if you are getting a laptop or Mac. You can get the fastest computer speed and highest RAM for the best prices with a desktop computer, PC, "renewed". With limited RAM and CPU speed, your plug-ins will lock up on you. You will still need to bounce down tracks with plug-ins, but you will not have to bounce down right away.

By the way, my prior "renewed" Dell computer that I purchased from Amazon is still working perfectly in my recording studio.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
The OptiPlex 7050 Micro turns out to be a surprisingly capable little lab box, especially when you throw Linux on it and let it breathe. The i7-6700T may be older, but paired with 32GB of RAM, it handles Docker stacks, lightweight VMs, home-lab services, and general experimentation without breaking a sweat. For a machine roughly the size of a sandwich, it’s shockingly stable under continuous workloads—something you notice when it’s been running for days without a hiccup or thermal complaint.

In practice, it makes an excellent “utility node” for the kind of mixed tasks labs tend to accumulate: small containers, automation tools, monitoring agents, or a handful of personal services. And yes—it even runs a Minecraft server just fine. The kids don’t care that the CPU launched during the Obama administration; they care that it doesn’t lag when someone decides to dump 12 stacks of TNT. The SSD and RAM make the whole setup feel modern, and Linux has no trouble with the hardware, meaning you spend your time deploying things—not troubleshooting drivers.

Limitations are predictable and manageable: no GPU means anything graphics-heavy is off the table, and CPU-bound workloads will eventually remind you this isn’t a workstation-class chip. But for a quiet, low-power lab machine that sits on a shelf and just handles whatever odd job you give it, the 7050 Micro punches well above its weight. It’s one of those “why didn’t we repurpose these sooner?” machines—cheap to source, easy to maintain, and perfect for homelab and testing environments.

Pros
• Handles Linux, Docker, and small services extremely well
• 32GB RAM = plenty of headroom for containers and light VMs
• Quiet, low power, and stable under long uptimes
• Great for kid-friendly game servers (Minecraft, Valheim Lite, etc.)
• Inexpensive and plentiful on the refurb market

Cons
• Skylake CPU will bottleneck heavy multi-container or CI workloads
• No dedicated GPU limits certain lab scenarios
• Limited storage expansion (one M.2 slot)
• Not suitable for large databases or high-throughput services

title: 4.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I purchased a used DELL OptiPlex 3020 SFF Desktop PC as a retired office computer for a family member to handle basic tasks like checking emails, browsing social media, and watching online videos. Overall, it’s been a reliable choice for the price, but it’s not without a few quirks.
The OptiPlex 3020 is a compact, no-frills machine that fits perfectly in a small home setup. Its performance is more than adequate for lightweight tasks—emails load quickly, social media scrolling is smooth, and streaming videos on platforms like YouTube or Netflix works well without buffering (assuming a decent internet connection). The small form factor is a big plus, as it doesn’t take up much space on the desk, and it runs quietly, which is great for a shared living space.
Since it was a used office PC, it came with a clean Windows install, and setup was straightforward. The system handles basic multitasking fine, like having a browser with a few tabs open while streaming music or videos. The included ports (USB, HDMI, VGA) made it easy to connect to a monitor and peripherals, which was a relief for a non-tech-savvy family member.
However, there are a couple of reasons it’s not a 5-star purchase. Being a used unit, the exterior had some minor scuffs and wear, which isn’t a dealbreaker but worth noting. More importantly, it can feel sluggish if too many browser tabs or apps are open at once, especially with heavier websites. The lack of modern upgrades like an SSD (mine came with an HDD) means boot times and app loading can be a bit slow, though this is expected for an older, budget-friendly machine.
For a refurbished office PC, the DELL OptiPlex 3020 SFF does exactly what we need for basic family use. It’s a cost-effective option for email, social media, and video streaming, but don’t expect it to handle anything beyond light tasks. If you’re looking for an affordable, dependable desktop for simple needs, this is a great pick—just consider upgrading to an SSD for a smoother experience!

I had to update to Windows 10 from Windows 7 and I found this refurb for about the same price as Windows 10 Pro on it's own. I went a step up from Amazon's Best Seller because I wanted dual displays and I liked how many USB ports were on this one.

First of all, ordered on Sunday or Monday and it said I would have it Friday. It was on my porch on Tuesday! And, it was in a nice box with really good packing.

I was pretty impressed with the insides...nice and neat and a good heatsink on the CPU. There were also a couple of extra programs installed that are probably freeware, but it was a nice touch. My copy of Windows had no issues. I did not have to contact tech support at all.

I originally picked up one of these micro pc's, but it was a little lacking in hard drive space, memory, and ports and was $60 more.

Being someone who has been building my own computers for 25 years, I was really happy with my purchase, but there were just a couple of things that would have made it 5 stars...

The case was a little damaged, so the front face is a little loose in the top corner (don't really care, but that's something somebody would gripe about). Also one of the PCM slots on back did not have a cover plate, which can let a lot of dust in...

I would have rather a RF keyboard/ mouse combo vs hardwired USB or not had a keyboard or mouse at all. I have a few extra parts around so I didn't need that and I will just give them away or pitch them, so I would have rather paid a little less or had some other things upgraded for the same price.

I would have preferred 16gb or ram even if it was a little more. 8gb is plenty, but I'm just sayin'.

I would have preferred a SSD hard drive vs SATA even if that meant 256gb vs 500 gb for that price point.

The computer has 2 display ports and a VGA. I would have liked 1 HDMI, 1 display port, and 1 VGA for the options, mostly because you have to do analog audio. This wouldn't be ideal if I wanted to use it as a media server.

All in all, nice computer for the price and it will handle my needs. I spent a lot of time going through options and I need to get this going. If the same company has a similar model with the comments above in mind I would be interested in getting another to replace my media center computer.

title: 1.0 out of 5 stars
text:
Purchasing a new computer should be a straightforward and satisfying experience, especially when buying a pre-configured system from a well-known brand like Dell. Unfortunately, my recent purchase of the Dell OptiPlex 5050 SFF from Green Tech Computers via Amazon has been anything but. What was supposed to be a reliable mini-server for my home office turned into a costly and frustrating ordeal filled with endless troubleshooting, unhelpful customer service, and a product that remains completely unusable.

Below, I’ve outlined my entire experience in detail to ensure others are aware of the challenges I faced and can make an informed decision before purchasing from this seller.

Initial Impressions and Setup
When I first received the Dell OptiPlex 5050 SFF, I was optimistic. The compact design and reputation of the OptiPlex series made it a great fit for my intended use as a mini-server for home projects. However, my optimism quickly faded once I powered on the machine.

From the start, I encountered a critical issue: the system was completely non-functional for basic tasks. I was unable to open browsers, download files, or install any updates. This wasn’t a minor glitch or software hiccup—these are basic functions that any modern computer, let alone a Dell-branded device, should be able to perform right out of the box.

Troubleshooting and Escalation
Recognizing that this wasn’t a typical setup issue, I began an extensive troubleshooting process to identify and resolve the problem. Below is a detailed timeline of my efforts:

1. Initial Troubleshooting Steps
I started by testing the system with standard diagnostics:

Ran Dell Diagnostics: The diagnostics tool reported no hardware issues, which suggested that all components were functioning as intended. However, this was contradicted by the ongoing problems.
Reinstalled Windows: Thinking the issue might be related to the pre-installed OS, I performed a clean installation of Windows 10. Unfortunately, the problems persisted. I couldn’t open browsers, download files, or install updates even after a fresh OS install.
Tested with Linux: I attempted to install Linux as an alternative operating system to bypass potential Windows-related issues. To my shock, the system wouldn’t even proceed to the installation stage, halting abruptly without any clear explanation. The live environment also failed to load. Ubuntu versions16.04, 22.04, 24 and PopOS were used.
2. Communication with Green Tech Computers
Frustrated, I reached out to the seller, Green Tech Computers, for assistance. This began a long and fruitless exchange, documented as follows:

Initial Contact (Dec 21, 2024): I informed them of the 0x80010105 error I was encountering and detailed the issues I was facing. Their response was to apologize and suggest replacing the hard drive, implying that the device had shipped with defective hardware. This was alarming—why would a new product require immediate hardware replacement?

Follow-Up Responses: Over the next several days, I provided them with screenshots of error messages and explained my troubleshooting efforts, including reinstalling Windows and attempting to update drivers. Their replies were repetitive and unhelpful. They insisted that the issue was a missing driver and suggested steps like installing updates via the store or resetting Windows Update components. None of these worked, as the system wouldn’t allow driver installations or updates to proceed.

Contradictory Advice: After reporting the continued failure of their suggestions, they shifted their diagnosis to a "defective system file" or a "Windows activation error." They advised me to download and reinstall Windows from Microsoft’s website—a step I had already performed multiple times without success.

3. Hardware Replacement Attempts
At their suggestion, I replaced the hard drive and memory with new components. I then performed another clean installation of Windows using verified installation media. Despite this, the exact same issues persisted, proving that the problem was not related to the hard drive, memory, or installation media. This confirmed that the root cause was likely a fundamental flaw in the system’s hardware or firmware.

Escalating Frustration
Poor Customer Service from Green Tech Computers
One of the most frustrating aspects of this experience was the lack of accountability or meaningful support from Green Tech Computers. Their responses were generic, dismissive, and showed little regard for the time and effort I invested in troubleshooting their faulty product. Even after replacing hardware and documenting every step of my process, their only advice was to repeat steps I had already tried or refer me back to Amazon.

Warranty Denial
To make matters worse, they refused to honor the warranty, claiming that the system was outside the 90-day warranty period. This was particularly upsetting as the delay in addressing the issue was due to customs clearance, which was beyond my control. I explained this to them and requested some leniency given the circumstances, but they flatly refused to provide any assistance, leaving me with an unusable system and no recourse.

Key Issues with the Product and Seller
1. Defective Hardware
The core problem with this system appears to be a defect in the hardware or firmware. Despite extensive troubleshooting, including replacing components and reinstalling operating systems, the system remains non-functional. This raises serious concerns about the quality control standards at Green Tech Computers.

2. Misleading Support
Throughout my correspondence with Green Tech Computers, their advice was inconsistent and unhelpful. They repeatedly blamed the issue on missing drivers or corrupted files without offering a concrete resolution. Their unwillingness to escalate the issue or take responsibility was unacceptable.

3. Warranty Limitations
Refusing to honor the warranty due to a minor delay caused by customs is an example of poor customer care. Given that the system was clearly defective from the start, Green Tech Computers should have taken ownership of the issue and offered a replacement or refund.

4. Financial Loss
In addition to the cost of the system itself, I incurred additional expenses for replacement hardware (hard drive and memory) and hours of lost time trying to resolve the issue. The total financial and emotional toll of this experience far exceeds the value of the product.

text:
I was a bit dubious about ordering this machine as the price seemed to good to be true and it was not available with Prime. I chose the free shipping option and it arrived much faster than predicted - no HST or duties payable on receipt. It was sent form the USA.

It was packed very well and the machine was very clean, the only defect that I could see was that there was a tiny ding in the case otherwise it was in perfect condition.

I ordered the Win11 version with 32GB of memory and a 512GB NVMe drive. In retrospect, I discovered that if I had chosen the Win10 version then I could have ordered it with 64GB of memory and a 1TB NVMe drive. I would have done that if I had realised that at the time, but I can add more memory later if I wish so matter.

My machine did come with on-board wifi and Bluetooth and it also came with a DVD-RW which I was not expecting. There was also the inevitable wired keyboard and mouse.

I like Dell business computers like this, they are solid and workmanlike, are not stuffed with crap software and, most importantly, Dell publishes very detailed online manuals on how to service and upgrade their hardware.

I will be using this computer mostly for software development and running a Linux VM so having lots of memory will be good.

I have been using the machine for a few weeks now with no problems and it is much faster then the Dell Optiplex 5050 that it replaces.

All in all, I am very happy with my purchase and will check out ReUse computers next time I am looking for an upgrade.

BTW. As stated, this version of the 7090 has a 10th generation Intel processor in it, a slighty later version of the 7090 has an 11th generation processor which would allow you to use somewhat faster NVMe drives (4 lanes versus 3). Otherwise I don't think that it makes a significant difference.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
For the first 24 hours, I was really impressed. Really snappy performance, 8 GB of RAM was plenty for simple tasks, and the SSD was capacious at 256 GB, considering the price. The inclusion of Windows Pro made the box almost free! However, after updating to Windows 11 Build 22H3, during the process of applying updates, the computer locked up. After 60 minutes with the computer no longer visible on the network and the keyboard and mouse non-responsive, pulled the power cord. Upon restoring power and turning on the computer, the PC was stuck for hours at the spinning circle during boot.

Two more power-cycles and Windows repair interface appeared. Selected Windows Reset, Local Source (wouldn't work with cloud source), Windows began resetting. However, after a restart, computer back to the infinitely spinning circle. :-(

If this had proved reliable, I'd have bought a dozen or more as remote monitoring PCs for client networks. But given that I've had good luck with the similarly priced AWOW models, I will not be investing any more money or time in the GMKTek offerings.

Update 01-07-2024
-----------------------

Fortunately, GMKTek provides a download for a Windows 11 re-installation ISO. With this and leveraging a fair amount of knowledge of Windows installation options, was able to re-image the SSD. Unfortunately, the product key is invalidated and I had to use a spare Windows 10 product key to re-activate Windows. Unfortunate the GMKTek hasn't worked out the same relationship with Microsoft that Dell has, whereby any Windows 11 ISO used to load Windows onto a Dell OptiPlex results in an automatically activated Windows 11 installation.

Bottom line is that after recreating and updating all apsects of the re-installed Windows 11 OS, the PC is back to running normally. I know to steer clear now of some driver updates. The PC has been running for about 36 hours and I'll post an update if that changes in the near future.

When this PC works, it represents a great value for the money in terms of hardware specs and a Windows 11 license. However, taking into account the time issue remediation takes and the expertise required, the TCO (total cost of ownership) rises significantly. If I never have to do brain surgery on this device again, I'll still feel the cost was justified based on the performance of this sub-$200 device.

P.S. I now make a complete image backup before running/installing ANY updates so I can simply restore the image backup rather than running into yet another Windows 11 re-installation process and the requirement to use/purchase another Windows product key.

P.P.S. The WIndows 11 re-installation ISO download was 11 GB and was not a standard Windows 11 installation ISO. This had to be burned to a flash drive (I used a 16 GB USB3 model; I used Rufus to create the bootable UEFI flash drive) and then the GMKTek PC booted with it. Upon boot, I was faced with a terminal window and a couple of choices. The one I chose led to an image/sysprep process that fortunately got the PC bootable once again with Windows 11 Pro.

P.P.P.S. Highly recommended --> As soon as you boot the device for the first time, find a tool such as ProduKey by NirSoft and extract and save the Windows 11 product key. Ideally (although I didn't have a chance to test), this key would work if a re-install was ever required. The other option, that I was waiting for until the PC was fully updated, is to create an image backup using any number of tools, including the image backup tool in Windows. Thus, if any of your update processes results in a non-bootable PC, you can simply re-image from the backup and avoid having a non-activated instance of Windows 11.

Update 01-12-2024
-----------------------

Vendor reached out proactively and offered some assistance, although I'd resolved the corrupt Windows 11 issue independently. However, that level of customer support is remarkable considering the price of this product and the lack of such support from other vendors with much pricier offerings. Due to this, upgrading the rating to four stars.

Update 01-13-2024
-----------------------

Customer support proactively reached out and provided a product key so I could activate Windows 11 and free up my personal product key. GMKtec's proactive reaching out to a customer with issues is almost unparalleled in my experience over 40 years, so despite the issues I encountered, I'm raising my review to five stars. For a product this inexpensive but with excellent performance, providing this level of customer support is laudable.

The old PC was used mainly for internet researches, some homework related uses, some attempts in coding and writing emails etc. A Steam client was running on it with quite a collection, but more casual games. text:
Very nice PC for the money! Fast processor and excellent Nvidia graphics card. Very quiet fan operation. Plenty of fast USB3 ports, front and back. Cool looks.

Mine came with Windows 10 pre-installed and fully functional, but no Windows 10 "activation code". So at first it seems that Windows 10 cannot be activated properly on this machine. I noticed that there is no Windows 10 documentation anywhere in the paperwork that came with my PC. When you go to the Microsoft web site to register it, it says the PC's serial number is not registered for Windows 10, and they send you to a site to pay $120 for a Windows 10 Home license. Also, a watermark is seen on the lower right corner of your screen telling you your Windows 10 is not activated. Lack of Windows activation has given me problems in getting Office 365 to work, since the machine is currently unlicensed according to Microsoft. The Amazon description claims it comes with Windows 10 Home - which is only partially true due to the above situation. In fact, it may be an un-licensed copy. Might have to buy that license at some point.

EDIT : Found the Windows 10 Product key !! by opening PowerShell and typing this command :
wmic path SoftwareLicensingService get OA3xOriginalProductKey
and then pasting the long product key (make sure you write it down for future reference) into the PC Settings > Update>Activation window. All is good now !!

EDIT 2 : I am looking for a memory upgrade, right now it comes with 8+8=16GB of DDR4 2666MHz 288pin ram. I plan to use two sticks of 32GB ram, for a total of 64GB. The memory I am looking at is : Crucial Ballistix 3200 MHz DDR4 DRAM Desktop Gaming Memory Kit (288pin) 64GB (32GBx2) CL16 BL2K32G32C16U4R (RED), or https://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B083TRRT1N/ref=ox_sc_act_title_1?smid=ATVPDKIKX0DER&psc=1

Hopefully that should work straight out of the box !

Really happy with my purchase, the M8 is a little workhorse. I can confirm it comes with an activated Win 11 Pro. Even though GMK has never seen an issue, I have a ritual - I boot from USB and image the NVME fresh (after getting the Windows key from a command line just in case), then wipe the mini pc's NVME (deleting all partitions) and install Windows 11 fresh. Windows picked up the BIOS key automatically on install and launched right into a fresh Windows 11 Pro. Network and sounds drivers were missing, but I grabbed them from the Europe site (Google it) and ran the .bat file. Without a reboot, everything picked up and no yellow exclamation marks in Device Manager. Windows Update took about 20 mins, as I fresh installed the newest Win 11 version (25H2 as of this writing).

So the PC itself is rock solid, no blue screens, streams OBS 4k just fine, and have no random crashes or reboots. It's a great Docker server or workstation PC if needed, runs Office just fine. I notice no loud fan noise. Can’t comment on Oculink, I don’t use it.

If you're looking for an all-in-one on the Ryzen platform, this one is a good bang for the buck.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
NOTE: My usage does not involve gaming. I wanted a smaller PC for office use, surfing and monitoring one surveillance camera.

The Good: Very compact, I was surprised at how small it is. Can easily pick it up and lift it with one hand. I most definitely got the "Mini" version (i.e. not just Small Form Factor). What I received is 2" larger in 2 dimensions compared to a 5X5 NUC (Next Unit of Computing form factor). Zippy performance on this HP with a Core i5 2.5 Ghz CPU. (Perspective: For YouTube 1080p and general surfing, this HP 800 Elitedesk feels as fast as my other PCs which are i7-4790K with 16GB RAM PCs that have top quality Solid State Drives). Boots quickly. No overheating. Once I started using it, I said to myself "Why do people even bother with Intel (or AMD) NUCs? (i.e. the 5X5" "Next Unit of Computing" form factor). From what I read, many of the people that go with NUC sized units have nothing but overheating and driver problems. None of that here with this HP unit.

256GB Fast SSD drive but after formatting and putting windows on it, you get 233GB - still pretty good.

Totally silent. Many USB 3.0 ports.

The Bad: No HDMI out. It has Display Port and VGA. ( I ordered a DP to HDMI adapter. We'll see. For now I'm using VGA as a workaround.)

No Operating System disk as a fail safe if I needed to do a reinstall / repair. No OS image on USB drive, or recovery partition (that I can find) provided on the SSD drive. No papers or instructions of any kind - which doesn't bug me that much but no license key is a bit annoying. You boot as Local Adminstrator with a "Null" (blank set) password. I immediately reset it and created other accounts for daily use.

There are many Amazon "resellers" of this HP. I deliberately chose one with a 100% rating and paid 40 - 50 dollars more for that. I can say that the computer I received is what was actually pictured/listed/presented. Mine arrived packaged well and came with basic keyboard and mouse. ABSOLUTELY NO BLOATWARE.. YAY! So far, I am very pleased with what I got. I think if you were to buy from a lowball (bottom price or rating) you are asking for trouble. YMMV.

I can definitely recommend this PC...IF ...what you receive is what is pictured/presented fulfilled from a reliable Amazon reseller (sub vendor?). Again, I was pleasantly surprised by the performance and value I got. In the future I may give up on custom build-my-own full sized PCs.

UPDATE: My SSD (Solid State Drive) died after 6 months. It was an off brand, but for the time it worked it was very fast. PC abruptly became unbootable, the "hard drive" utility check in the BIOS confirmed it was dead.

THE BAD NEWS: I had to order a replacement drive as I was way beyond the resellers 90 day warranty. I stepped up to a Samsung 870 SATA SSD drive.

THE GOOD NEWS: In their defense, they pointed out that my Windows 10 install key was embedded in the PC - presumably in the BIOS firmware. This saved me $140 on the purchase of a new copy of Windows 10 Pro. All I had to do is find a spare USB drive (8GB minimum, I used a verbatim 16GB USB), go to the Microsoft Windows 10 download site. I did ** NOT ** chose the ISO option. The software was literally placed on the USB drive ready to go. When I power cycled it, Windows 10 installer came up and NEVER prompted me for a license key! Yay! And once install was completed, there is no prompt for activation.

text:
Stay away from Tek Refurbs. Full stop.
I ordered 10 refurbished Dell systems for the church where I work, expecting uniform, business-class machines suitable for deployment. What I received was a bait-and-switch disaster.
Every single unit had a replacement motherboard that did not match the model sold. These were not minor revisions — they were entirely different platforms stuffed into the wrong chassis. As a result:
BIOS updates for the advertised model cannot be applied
Chipset and firmware updates must be guessed and manually matched to the actual motherboard
Dell will not provide correct drivers because the service tag no longer matches the hardware
Systems appear functional at first glance but break in subtle, time-consuming ways (USB devices, cameras, firmware management, etc.)
Out of the box, these machines were not fit for business use. They were either unusable or required hours upon hours of deep technical troubleshooting per machine just to reach basic stability. This is completely unacceptable for equipment marketed as refurbished business desktops.
This isn’t normal refurbishment. This is Frankenstein hardware — mismatched boards, wrong firmware paths, and no supportability. If you’re not an experienced systems engineer with time to burn, these machines will waste your time, your money, and your sanity.
Tek Refurbs refused to take responsibility once outside their short return window, despite the issue being hardware misrepresentation, not wear and tear. They are great with copy/pasting the notice that I was outside the return window. No integrity whatsoever though.
If you value:
your time
consistent hardware
the ability to update BIOS and drivers
or any form of vendor accountability
Do not buy from Tek Refurbs.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I was looking for a second PC to run two twitch streams (DashDucks and OurChickenLife) to take the load off of my actual gaming laptop and possibly some light gaming. My initial reaction was this is surprisingly fast for a sub $125 mini PC. It is snappy and loads chrome and the two twitch streams just fine with each stream in a separate window (one on each monitor). I was super happy with finally having the ability to have a PC with dual monitors and at this price point is in incredible.

Set up was easy and I was up and running in under 5 minutes. Boot time is under 20 seconds and once I configured it for not needing to login even faster than that. I initially installed Steam, Discord, Chrome, SpeedTest (from the Microsoft store), and an auto clicker mouse program. I ended up deleting Steam and Discord as the game I primarily play struggled even on very low graphics settings. The game in question is Farm Together 2 and would highly recommend if you like farming games. Anyways, it wasn't unbearable but there was noticeable lag when moving around in the game. Discord ran ultra smooth though and there wasn't any lag so would be great for using that on this PC.

As for internet speeds and quality goes, I would very HIGHLY recommend using an ethernet cable if you can. My current internet speed is 1.0 GB up and down. Under WiFi, I got a 1/5th of that speed with speeds around 200 down and 150 up despite this PC being literally inches from the router. This is most likely a limit of the WiFi 5 used in this PC and not necessarily a defect. Once I installed a Cat 6 ethernet cable, I got around my full speed of 930 both up and down. While it was on WiFi, I didn't notice any lag when watching the twitch streams When installing windows updates though, definitely use an ethernet cable.

As for noise level this thing is ultra quiet even under 100% CPU usage. Always was cool to the touch when I checked and no burning or any kind of smells like that since I have been using it. I keep it running 24/7 and as of the writing of this review it has been flawless.

As for storage and RAM this seems to be good to go right out of the gate. You do have the option to upgrade if you wish, but for my needs the 8GB of RAM is just fine. It hits around 60% usage for RAM with running 2 chrome windows. And for storage with only chrome, speedtest, my mouse program, and edge which was preinstalled storage is very sufficient for me. And you can also upgrade the hard drive (SSD) to 2TB so if in the future I need more space or change how I use this PC I can. And honestly, that is a comforting thought knowing the option is available to me. If you are considering one of the larger storage models I would say go for it versus this 256GB version as it won't be an issue later on, but for me I got this version initially because of budget reasons and it would work for me and my needs. My game would probably run alot better if it had the 16GB of RAM but I am okay with just using it as a media consumption PC.

Not having to worry about batteries and all that jazz was a huge selling point for me versus getting, say a Chromebook. I have this plugged into my battery backup in the event of a power failure which alleviates my worries a bit.

My only real complaint with this PC is the placement of the power button. I did accidentally press it causing the PC to go to sleep when connecting my mouse and keyboard, but this can be changed in settings as to what the power button does in settings. I do wish it was in the front, but it isn't anything deal breaking.

Overall, this is a great little PC for what I needed it for, which was to run 2 twitch streams via chrome. Your mileage may vary, but I feel confident recommending this PC for light to medium use. I don't do video editing or any intense operations like that so I can't comment on that. USB connections have been stable (no random disconnects) and the HDMI ports have both been running great. It runs Windows 11 just fine and aside from some user stumbles on figuring out where things are now and then (coming from Windows 10) it is just fine.

I hope this review has helped you and have a blessed day <3

The manual is silent on how to do this, and I had forgotten on how I previously did this on other machines, so I emailed support@kamrui.com; result: Nada. (However, I finally remembered the crucial step --See below.) 2 Stars.
Placing greater emphasis on the five-star product itself, my overall rating is 4 stars

Note: The key step in creating a dual boot system is to access the American Megatrends (AMI) 5.26 BIOS immediately at startup. (I did this by repeatedly pressing the Esc and delete keys -- One of them works.) Once the BIOS display appears, move to the Boot tab and change the boot device order to place "USB Boot Device" first before the hard disk containing windows. Then insert a thumbdrive containing the Ubuntu OS into a USB port, click "Save & Exit" in the BIOS, and keep going.
