title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I live in a more remote location where most bargain places (recyclers, etc) won't ship at all, or want crazy $$ to ship. So this review is partially based on my limited choices... but I like this machine enough that I'd probably buy it anyway. This is perfect for the general office use I need it for.

First of all, the one I have up on my workbench now is exactly as the ad says. CPU, RAM, SSD are all correct, and test OK. Also, the machine is a lot newer than I expected. This one has a "born on" date of May 16, 2021. Based on the CPU, I was thinking it'd be a bit older.

The inside looks very very clean. Almost immaculate. The ad does not specify an optical media drive but the chassis can accommodate a slim (laptop size) drive, if you want to add one.

The shipping box was a simple affair with very strong inflated padding inside. I suggest they use a bit more tape, but the box arrived ok. Inside, there was the PC, plus power cable, USB adapters for WiFi and BT, Keyboard and Mouse, and an adapter for DP to HDMI. Really a thoughtful combination. Just make sure to look through the entire box, as these items are loose. [A small baggy for these, taped to the machine would be good idea]

Before trying to power on, I opened the case to make sure RAM wasn't jostled loose during transit or the CPU cooler hadn't come off somehow. All was fine. On powering up, my machine sputtered a bit (on/off itself a couple times) and complained about a loss of date/time. This is normal for when the CMOS battery is too low/dead. I switched it out for a good battery and all works well. (This may be frustrating for some buyers, but if you leave the machine plugged in, it won't need the battery anyway until there's a power outage)

I'm ordering 2 more and will probably order more later on too. It's a 5-star product. Maybe a wee tiny bit expensive for big metro areas, but a great deal for me where I am.

EDIT: I've now ordered quite a few of these, and the price is better than ever. Some had SSD (SATA) and some NVMe. One had an optical drive. There's a relatively recent BIOS update too. I believe this vendor is merely following the correct MS **requirements** for selling refurbished machines which generally requires putting the original OS version back in it's initial state for a new user, and must include a kyb/mouse.

The box is very tight and usable. I'd don't use the front usb ports but can definitely use more of those in the back or the sides. Alas, usb-c would have been better and easier to fit on this small form factor. Including for the display.

The box is plenty powerful. Besides its form factor and power consumption (~10w at idle), there is nothing mini about it. It runs everything shot of image rendering games with ease. Cooling is quite efficient. There is no noise at all. At 20C ambient temperature, the cpu stays under 50C while playing YT videos full screen at 4k. It comes pre-imaged with windows 11 which is convenient. However, reinstalling standard windows (any version) is a lost cause. The way to re-install the operating system, esp if it gets corrupted, is to re-image the ssd with a custom image of windows 11 provided by the manufacturer.

text:
Very nice little package which installs Win11 Pro on first boot (need wired ethernet). I now have 2 of them providing Plex server for TVs and backup for other computers. Quiet and cool.
It has 2 slots each for memory and m.2 SSD disk. I got the 16 gb + 1 TB configuration, then added a 2 TB SSD in the second slot. Now I have 3 TB total with 1 TB system disk and 2 TB data disk.
One system had a single 16 gb memory card while the other had two 8 gb. I replaced an 8 gb card with 16 gb and now have 24 gb in each.
It is a little tricky doing the upgrade. Remove feet, then with small phillips remove screws. You may have to slap a corner in your hand to get them out of the hole. Pull the back slightly from cover and use a card to run around the edge. Work to pull the insides from case. Do not jerk as there are a couple wire to the case. Add SSD and memory at top. The tricky part is the power button. Put cover on side with power down and place in case. Then slide computer in. Make sure it fits to edges and you can see all connectors, then re-screw.

text:
I got this a couple weeks ago and have been playing with it since. I have to admit, I really love this Mini PC trend. It's powerful and quiet and does everything a bigger system can do.
Unboxing the system was simple. All the components were inside and felt secure. It came with the computer, a power cable, HDMI cable, instructions, and screws with a small mounting bracket (e.g. to attach it to a monitor). When it's powered on, it has a nice blue glow, which makes my desk look really mystical in the dark, or has just enough light to let me know it's on.
It has a decent amount of ports - two HMDI, which can support 4k monitors (mine are only 1080p), two USB3 ports, two USB2 ports, a wired network port, and a combined microphone/speaker port. One thing I love is how the main body splits - you can put a laptop hard drive in it for extra storage, like large video or game files, or use it slim.
It comes with Windows 11 pro, which is ready out of the box. Edge and Chrome ran without complaining, serving up any web page I could find. I wanted to see if this system could handle Linux, so I put Ubuntu on it, and I think it runs even better than Windows, although I'm going to stick with Windows for casual gaming purposes.
I can see this being useful for a home office or basic gaming, and at the price, it feels perfect for a holiday gift... but I'm keeping this for myself. Get your own.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
This little computer is a bargain for a desktop system or an HTPC. It has plenty of compute power for an small office or home PC. It can even run some low end 3D games, although you might have to turn down the graphics settings in the games. All you need is a monitor along with a Display Port to HDMI cable for a complete setup. You can download OpenOffice or LibreOffice for an effective office software suite. It is one of the most inexpensive ways that you can get a Windows 11 compatible computer.

Any time you buy one of these refurbished systems, and i have bought a few, you can expect some minor variations in configuration from what is stated. They usually give you more rather than less (which would annoy buyers). Mine came as advertised with the one exception that it has a 3400G processor that is a bit faster than the 3400GE, but that draws 65W of power instead of 35W. I would have preferred the lower wattage GE for my application, but it is fine. Internally, it came with a Toshiba 256GB M.2 NVMe SSD, an Intel AX210 M.2 WiFI/BT card, and a single Micron Technology 8GB DDR4 2666 SODIMM memory card.

It has a empty removable tray for a 2.5" SATA HD or SSD. You have to remove that tray to get to the M.2 slots underneath. It is a bit harder to remove that tray than it is on the 800 G2 or 805 G5 that I also own. it is only more difficult because there are cables both front and back on it. The back is the SATA ribbon cable and the front is the fan cable. I think the safest way to remove it is to first remove the SATA connector from the tray carefully so that you don't pull the ribbon cable out of its connector on the board - which wouldn't be the end of the world, but they are obnoxious to reinsert. Then you pull off the front screw. slide the tray forward, lift it up and out, then rotate it towards the front to not pull out the fan connector. BTW, mine came with the SATA ribbon cable already pulled out of the board - perhaps the only minor complaint I had.

Because there is no HDD in the tray, you do not get the special bushings it takes to mount a drive there. But, I found that drone M3 anti-vibration standoffs, such as the ones from FPVDrone, work well enough. You can find them here on Amazon.

If you hold down ESC when you boot it, it goes into the BIOS. In that BIOS are diagnostics to run that you can use to check out your computer. I recommend that you do so before installing the OS. Mine passed just fine. You also might want to go through the settings. I couldn't get mine to boot from a USB stick until I checked the box in the BIOS to allow that. Businesses often lock down USB ports for security reasons, and these PCs come out of businesses that have moved on to more current computers.

If you are looking for a low cost way to get a computer for non-gaming usage, this is a great value.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
In my real life, I am a Technical Writer and Knowledge Manager for the company I work for, so if this review seems a little long or maybe too detailed, I wanted to make sure you got as much information as possible as I started using the computer. At home I am an avid movie and personal video collector and I just completed rebuilding my video server. It is in a tower case and is occupying the only space I have in my office for such a computer. As part of the rebuild, I intended to separate the serving and processing functions, so I was searching for a compact solution that would allow me to render video content for the server. This computer has provided everything I was looking for and more.

These are the criteria I used in deciding on a replacement computer

High speed processing
I needed a computer that would help with video rendering. I am not a gamer but the performance of a gaming computer would speed up the video work I do. With the initial testing, this design is completing the rendering tasks about 20% faster that my previous computer.

A compact Design.
I have limited space on my desk for a PC. This mini PC was great as the size gave me options on my already crowded desk. Its size allowed me to place it behind a monitor, but there were also 2 mounting screw holes in the case so I decided to mount it to the back of my desk.

Convenience of Several connection options.
With 4 USB A ports I was able to connect my printers, keyboard and mouse and still had USB C connection options for my USB monitor and an External SSD device. See the picture Exterior Pictures Showing Ports and Top Removal
Along with that connectivity there are options to connect wireless networks and to use Bluetooth top connect audio devices like headphones.

Expandability
In this small package I could still add an additional standard sized SSD. The surprise expandability is found in the Oculink Port this port gives PCIe connectivity speed for external devices.

What Came in the Box
The computer
Introductory Booklet (Unfortunately not an English Page, but other picture have some English labels.)
Power Supply and Power Cord
HDMI cable (Must boot first time on HDMI)
Mounting Bracket (No instructions on the exact uses. I mounted mine using the mounting holes on the back of the case.)
See the Picture What's In the Box

Setting up the Computer
Unpacking the computer was straight forward. There was no assembly required. The only things needed to get started is a monitor to connect the HDMI cable (provided), a keyboard & mouse and to plug in the power supply.
I followed the instructions on the yellow notice over the network ports advising that the system would set up much more quickly without Windows attempting to update during the initial boot up. This worked great and I will use this process on any other computer I will build. Within a few minutes, I was at the windows desktop. I was in a position to start installing software. See picture Original Desktop.
I then connected a network wire and I was able to install my software and connect to my Microsoft account.
There was a bit of disappointment, as there were no instructions in English supplied. There were about 10-12 languages in a pamphlet included in the box but none were English. The drawings were labeled well enough to identify the details of the ports well enough for my trained eye, but the standard user may be left with questions about a few of the ports.
I decided to add a second SSD to the computer and found the access inside very simple. Turned the top shield a quarter turn to the left and it unlocked exposing 4 screws that held the top fan in place. Once those were removed, the fan lifted out easily (be careful of the wire connecting the system board to the fan.)
See the picture Disassembly with SSD 2 Slot Identified
As part of the final setup, I had to decide where the computer would be on my desk. I had a option to put it behind my monitor See Picture Behind the Monitor, but instead, I took advantage of the mounting holes on the bottom of the computer to hang the computer from the back of my desk. See the picture Desk Mount

BIOS Notes
I did look at the BIOS. I was curious about how configurable it was as I have found with other units that the BIOS is very focused and not designed to allow tweaking. While the interface was not very fancy (very DOS like) it appeared to have several settings to adjust memory and processor. See the picture BIOS Advanced There are many drill down options.

Summary
Overall this computer provides a significant performance boost over the equipment I had. In my research I found that the AMD products provide better performance for the dollar, combined with integrating the GPU into the chip design it made the unit compact while still providing enough horsepower to drive 3 monitors effectively. In the few days I have worked with this unit, I still find myself marveling at how fast bootup times are and how quickly applications launch and web pages load. If you are looking for a gaming computer I would give this one a chance, I think you will be surprised at the speed of this computer and its ability to keep up with some of the most demanding games.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
This is specifically for the K12 with the Ryzen 7 H 255.

Honestly, not a bad deal.

The CPU is pretty good for its class, and has very acceptable integrated graphics. The H 255 is seemingly only sold to the chinese market, has no real documentation officially (as of the time of writing), and is essentially a recycled die from better chips that didn't meet the cut so to speak (at least as far as I can find), but I don't see any of those as a real problem; die recycling is perfectly fine if it actually works and is stable, and AMD is usually pretty good at the latter... and it makes me feel a little better that AMD can save something that would otherwise end up being e-waste. Despite the borderline unofficial nature of the CPU, I have not experienced any performance issues, instability, or crashes of any kind after a few weeks. Note that I updated the BIOS and microcode immediately after receiving the unit, and I suggest everyone do the same.

The unit itself is from GMKtec, which is a chinese company. However, there were some (good) surprises in the box that tells me they actually cared about the end user experience, though possibly only just enough to make sure that the average joe blow didn't immediately return it because they got pissed off at something that would honestly be Microsoft's fault (eg. the horrendous OOBE for Windows). I choose to believe they actually care though, and somewhat reinforcing that, my email to them was answered the next day (I'll get to what the contents of that was later).

The specs of the unit, aside from the CPU which is pretty good itself, are actually darn incredible. OCuLink is a quasi-rare connector, but an *extremely* welcome one! That significantly improves the unit's lifespan and enables mostly modern gaming, provided you genuinely do the research into how to use it (remember, don't plug or unplug it when the PC is on!), though it can already handle light-medium gaming with just the integrated graphics. Though I have not tried the OCuLink port yet, I have no reason to believe it doesn't work or anything like that. USB4 is also extremely welcome, and I can confirm that it not only works, but it follows best practices of how to implement the protocol. Since the port does do PCIe tunneling, it should work with all Thunderbolt 4 appliances out of the box. GMKtec could have taken the cheap way out and omitted this detail, but they did not. Absolutely incredible to have both of these available.

There are also, seemingly (I have not opened the unit up yet, no reason to), three M.2 slots, one at Gen4x4 and two at Gen4x2, which is perfectly fine in terms of speed and great in terms of how many slots they offer. I cannot think of any other mini PC with this level of overall connectivity. You lose out on some external USB connectors that would otherwise be present, but USB4 seriously more than makes up for it. The dual 2.5G LAN ports are just the whipped cream on top of all this.

Though, not all can be as good. There is no S3 power state support in the firmware, so you're stuck with shutting down the computer, hibernating it, or relying on Microsoft's absolutely abysmal "implementation" of sleep in the form of modern standby (S0). This was confirmed in my aforementioned email to GMKtec's support. Oh well, I have the whipped cream but miss out on the cherry. This may be an oversight on GMKtec's part, but it may also be difficulty getting S3 implemented with OCuLink. Don't know exactly how that works. I'm tempted to knock a star off for this, since S3 is a very, very nice power state to have available, but it's something I'm personally not terribly concerned about, especially with everything else so good. Please, if you're reading this GMKtec, add it in a BIOS update! Would love to see it!

There may also be an issue with the TPM, specifically in regards to when the firmware tells the OS to initiate S0 sleep (eg. from the power button short pressed). In such an event, when the computer resumes from S0 the TPM will either fail or lock up. This may be an issue with Windows, or with the TPM, or with just my unit, and it requires a reboot to clear it up. Either way, my way around it is to leave the unit turned on or to just shut it down, but again it's not a concern for me personally, and YMMV.

Overall, I would recommend this unit. Though I have not opened it to inspect the internals, nor tested the OCuLink connector yet, I see great value in this unit, and I imagine I will keep it around for a very long time, getting significant usage out of it. I would give it 4.5 stars if that were possible, but for Amazon I will leave it at 5.

First the good - There are several product reviews here and elsewhere so this will come as no surprise but this thing is TINY. My old NUC 7i5 seems like Goliath in comparison, and I used to think that it was David. The PC booted right up and the seller provided detailed instructions on initial setup without connecting to the internet, followed by restart and connecting to the internet to get updates. Setup went without a hitch. A full virus scan showed that it was clean and free of threats. The BIOS is the newer one (dated 5/21/2024) and allows setting the fan to its highest 5000+ rpm (was at "adaptive" out of the box - the fan is very quiet even at full), setting the GPU to its highest at 1200MHz (was at 900MHz out of the box), and setting the power draw at 15W (was at 12W out of the box). Works quite well and handles word documents, powerpoint presentations, excel spreadsheets, youtube videos and browsing with ease. The temps on the CPU and GPU are quite reasonable (~39C idle and ~50C with multiple browser windows open and streaming a 4K UHD movie. I'm not a gamer, so I can't attest to that aspect, but I suspect it will handle older games just fine.

Now the bad - Packing left a lot to be desired. No bubble wrap around the box - just the GMKtec miniPC product box in a brown envelope. The carrier (UPS) was not gentle with the package but thankfully the mini pc was unharmed during transit to me. Also, this appears to a documented issue, but on this particular machine, one (the one on the front further away from the power button) of the USB ports just does not work. It does not recognize anything plugged into it (wired or wireless keyboards, mice, flash drives etc.). This despite setting the power draw to 15W. The other two USB ports work fine. Given that there are only three USB ports on this mini pc, if you use a wired keyboard and a wired mouse, you won't have any available USB ports to plug in flash drives or other devices. You will be forced to buy a USB hub. It isn't a major issue for me, particularly given the price, but I wish GMKtec would address this recurring issue on this particular model once and for all.

As a home PC for everyday tasks this is a good bargain and if GMKtec would address the lack of better (bubble wrap around the box) packaging during shipping and the non-functional USB port, it would be a GREAT bargain. Four stars because of these two issues.

O desempenho do N97 com 12GB Ram consegue executar várias ações, exemplos: Ver videos em 1080p sem perda de frames, e para fins de testes executei o demo do RE 7 com uns 25 ~ 30 fps em 900p com opções no médio.

Vi na internet (Porém ainda não instalei) esse mesmo modelo executando emuladores de PS2 com taxa estável de 60fps em 720p.

Por fim eu sou usuário Linux e estou deixando esse mini pc como alternativa para alguns aplicativos que só funcionam no Windows, que por ventura acompanha a licença original. Porém sei que roda Linux também, mas no meu caso já tenho outras máquinas.

No geral, tem várias portas e conectividade: 3 x USB 3.0, Bluetooth, WIFI, LAN, SD e 2 HDMI.

É uma alternativa interessante de mini pc, com desempenho legal, baixo consumo de energia e não ocupa muito espaço.

I've bought 4 other refurbished Lenovo desktops and laptops over the years from other sources, and have found it to be a reliable brand (as have many surveys).
I was actually a bit reluctant to purchase this PC, because of the low price, but couldn't be happier with the result....

2. The instructions recommend setting up the included copy of Windows 11 without a Microsoft account (which I definitely concur with), but this could not be accomplished without the OOBE\BYPASSNRO command and a reboot (google it to see the procedure), so those instructions should be updated.

I've been both buying and building PCs since the early '90s, and overall, I couldn't be happier with this purchase, and will definitely consider MaxE Computers for future refurb purchases.

text:
Nachdem mein alter Stand-Pc zu langsam geworden ist, habe ich mich nach einem neuen Pc für Office arbeiten umgesehen. Da bin ich auf dieses kompakte Kraftpaket gestoßen. Ich war erst skeptisch ob der Prozessor genug Leistung bringt, aber nach einigen Tests bin ich äusserst positiv überrascht.
Der kleine Celeron aus der 11. Generation kommt mit 4 Kernen daher und hat einen Basistakt von 2 GHz. In der Realität kommt er aber dank Intel Turbo Boost 2.0 auf 2,6 GHz in kurzen Phasen sogar auf 2,9 GHz.
Ich hatte keinerlei Probleme was die Leistung angeht. Mein Gerät ist ausserdem mit 8GB RAM und 256 GB SSD Speicher ausgestattet. Das wirkt vielleicht auf den ersten Blick etwas klein, aber für das was ich damit anstelle reicht es mehr als aus.
Als Betriebssystem kommt Windows 11 vorinstalliert. Es gibt keine unnötigen vorinstallierten Programme, nur Windows.
Die Einrichtung war ziemlich einfach. Nach ca. 15 Minuten war alles fertig und der Pc einsatzbereit.
Ich habe auch ein paar kleine Benchmarks laufen lassen. Leistungstechnisch bewegt sich der Prozessor ca. bei halber Lestung eines i7 der 11. Generation. Das klingt erst mal mager, aber wie gesagt, für Büroarbeiten mehr als ausreichend.
Was die Grafikleistung angeht kommt hier eine Intel UHD Grafikeinheit zum Einsatz. Damit lassen sich bis theoretisch bis zu 3 4k@60Hz Monitore ansteuern. Allerdings gibt es nur 2 dedizierte Video Ausgänge.
Nach etwas rumprobieren kann ich sagen, dass Videowiedergabe von 4k Inhalten möglich ist, alles was über 4k hinaus geht ist dann aber doch zu viel. Aber als solide Media Station kann ich das kleine Ding auf jeden Fall auch empfehlen.

I/O ist für so ein kleines Gerät auch beachtlich:
Wir haben insgesamt 3 normale USB Typ-A und 2 USB Typ-C Schnittstellen. Die beiden USB-A Ports auf der Rückseite sind USB 3.1 Anschlüsse mit 5 Gbps, der auf der Front ist ein USB 3.2 mit 10 Gbps.
Bei den Typ-C Ports ist es anders herum. Auf der Vorderseite haben wir 5 Gbps und auf der Rückseite sind es 10 Gbps.
Ausserdem befindet sich auf der Rückseite noch ein Gigabit Ethernet Port, ein HDMI 1.4 und ein Mini DisplayPort (ein Adapter von Mini auf Voll sit dabei) und der Stromanschluss.
Auf der Vorderseite befindet sich neben den beiden USB Ports noch ein Kombo Kopfhörer-Mikrofon 3,5mm Klinke Anschluss und der Anschalter.
Auf der linken Seite befindet sich ein SD-Karten Leser und rechts haben wir ein Kenisington Lock. Wer seine Gräte gerne anschließt, kann das also auch tun ;)
Dazu gibt es dann noch Bluetooth und Wlan mit dabei, sodass man kein Lan-Kabel Quer durchs Hauslegen muss. Bislang gab es auch noch keine negativen Verbindungsabbrüche.

Was die Benutzung angeht bin ich echt beeindruckt. Selbst unter Vollast hört man nicht mehr als ein flüster-leises säuseln des Lüfters. Mein alter Stand Pc war deutlich lauter im Vergleich. Ein nettes Feature ist die VESA Halterung die mitgeliefert wird. Damit lässt sich der kleine Kasten sehr einfach auf die Rückseite von Monitoren, and die Wand oder unter den Schreibtisch hängen und ist somit einfach zu verstecken.
Mit einem Bluetooth Tastatur/Maus Set lässt sich so ein komplett kabelloser Schreibtisch einrichten - sehr schick, allerdings für mich nicht so wichtig.

Für alle die ihren Stromverbrauch senken wollen habe ich gute Neuigkeiten: Das kleine Teil braucht zwischen 8 und 20 Watt, je nach Auslastung natürlich.

Alles in allem bin ich wirklich zufrieden. Der Rechner ist klein, leise und für die Leistung echt günstig. Office Programme laufen ohne Probleme, Videos schauen (streamen oder von Platte) geht ohne Probleme. Wer keinen NASA Rechner braucht oder einen Gaming Pc sucht, der wird hiermit mehr als zufrieden sein.

text:
Este mini-PC es una pasada.

El producto, además del ordenador en sí, trae una funda, por si quieres llevarte el ordenador en una mochila, para que no se ralle. Trae también un cable HDMI, y una plaquita cuadrada con tornillos, para ponerla detrás de tu monitor (si tiene soporte VESA) y tener así un all-in-one (aunque claro, para meter y sacar pendrives podría quedar un poco a desmano).

En un tamaño súper compacto que te podrías meter en el bolsillo de un abrigo tienes un ordenador personal completo. La presentación es inmejorable, viene en una cajita compacta muy bien protegida. El diseño es muy bonito, la superficie es de color negro y brillante, puede dejar marcas de dedos pero no se ve especialmente "sucio" y además se limpia fácil. La calidad de materiales se hace patente en cuanto lo sacas de la caja. Tiene 3 USB normales, 2 USB-C, salida de auriculares, toma de red RJ45, mini Displayport y HDMI. También tiene una ranura de lector de tarjetas SD. El botón de Power se pone en naranja parpadeante cuando el equipo está en suspensión, es apretarlo y se enciende la pantalla de bloqueo de windows de forma instantánea.

El equipo en sí no es muy potente. Pero es que me ha costado poco más de 200€ cuando los modelos superiores i3, i5 o i7 están entre 300 y 600 euros. Obviamente para juegos o para meterle caña con temas gráficos seguramente no sea la mejor opción. Sin embargo sí que es más que suficiente para un uso diario normal, como para temas de ofimática, usar el Chrome para ver vídeos en youtube, navegar por redes como Facebook, instalar aplicaciones sencillas como Spotify, tener algún gestor de fotos, programitas no muy pesados, etc. El procesador muy raramente llega al 100%, y esto es algo que sorprende, pues los céleron antes iban muy limitados. Al parecer las nuevas versiones de los céleron van bastante más holgadas que antes.

De momento estoy impresionado y muy contento. Tengo conectado un monitor QHD de 1440 líneas y se ve súper nítido. Viene con el nuevo Windows 11, que se configura nada más encenderlo, en 5 minutos, y que me está resultando bastante atractivo.

text:
Mein Laptop ist nach zehn bis elf Jahre in sein Alter gekommen, um sich so langsam in Rente zu verabschieden. Daher habe ich schon seit längerer Zeit nach einem Ersatz gesucht und bin dabei auf die MiniPCs gestoßen. Da ich Tastatur und Monitore zur Erweiterung des Laptops schon habe und diese nicht wegwerfen will, habe ich mich mit dem Thema MiniPC befasst. Durch Zufall bin ich auf die Firma Geekom aufmerksam geworden und schwankte noch zwischen IT8 und IT11. Letzten Endes habe ich mich nun für den IT11 mit 16 GB RAM und 512 GB SSD entschieden. Ich bereue es kein bisschen und freue, dass ich nun auch endlich Windows 11 habe, da mein alter Laptop nicht Win11-fähig ist. Zudem kommt noch hinzu, dass ich durch den MiniPC wieder mehr Platz auf dem Schreibtisch habe.

Der MiniPC ist sehr handlich und kompakt gebaut, passt in meine Hand und ist leicht. Klar, Plastik bzw. Kunststoff ist dabei, doch sieht er hochwertig aus und die Verarbeitung, soweit es sich mir erschließt, ist auch sehr gelungen.

Anschlüsse sind mehr als genug vorhanden. An der linken Seite ist ein SD-Kartenslot vorhanden, an der rechten Seite ein Kensington Security Lock, was sicherlich auch bei dem ein oder anderen Verwendung finden wird. An der Vorderseite sind USB-C, USB-A, Klinkenanschluss und der Powerbutton. Hinten gibt es dem Stromanschluss, einen Mini DisplayPort, LAN-Anschluss, zwei USB-A, HMDI und USB-C. Alles in den neuesten Generationen und Variationen. Es sind genug Schnittstellen vorhanden, um allerlei Geräte anzuschließen. Ich gehe davon aus, dass man über HDMI und DisplayPort 4K rausbekommt und so ein sehr gutes Sehvergnügen hat. Offiziell sollen es bis zu vier 4K-Monitoren sein, da bin ich sehr gespannt, wenn ich mal dazu komme, meinen Schreibtisch soweit auszubauen und aufzurüsten.

Im Inneren ist es ein Intel-Chip i7 der 11. Generation verbaut, der meiner Meinung nach fast alle Wünsche für normaler (Office-)Anwendungen, außerhalb des Gamings, erfüllt. Die Testung als Media Server folgt, wenn ich alle Daten und Einstellungen vom Laptop auf dem MiniPC übertragen habe. Soweit ich gelesen habe, sind WiFi 6 und Bluetooth 5.2 mit an Bord. Mein Mobiltelefon (Samsung Galaxy) konnte ich problemlos über Bluetooth verbinden und das sogar einfacher und sehr viel schneller als mit meinem Laptop. Der Lüfter ist leise und vollbringt seine Arbeit.

Die Office Programme laufen flüssig und smooth und das Surfen im Netz ist bisher problemlos möglich, sogar mit vielen geöffneten Tabs. Windows 11 Pro ist schon vorinstalliert und das Starten und erstmalige Einrichten ging in unter sieben Minuten von statten, was mich überraschte und die Augen aufreißen ließ in Bezug auf Windows 11. Ich besitze den MiniPC erst seit etwa einer Woche, doch bin ich jetzt schon mehr als begeistert und zufrieden.

Die Möglichkeiten des Upgrades sind immens und ich werde nach und nach mit Sicherheit die Komponenten erweitern. Als erstes mit Sicherheit den Arbeitsspeicher, auch wenn der mit 16 GB erst einmal vollkommen ausreichend bemessen sein sollte. Allerdings fahre ich mittlerweile die Strategie, gleich hochzuzüchten, um hinterher meine Ruhe zu haben. Der Arbeitsspeicher (DDR4) ist laut Angabe bis auf 64 GB erweiterbar, was ich mir für die kommende Tage vorgenommen habe. Die SSD mit 512 GB mit dem Formfaktor 2280 ist bis auf 2 TB erweiterbar und zudem kann man noch in einem 2,5-Zoll-Schacht eine weitere SSD oder HDD mit SATA- oder PCI-Anschluss hinzufügen. Ausgelobt sind hierbei ebenfalls bis zu 2 TB. Dadurch hätte man 4 TB Speicher und dies sollte mehr als ausreichend sein und wenn einem doch noch etwas fehlt, einfach über einen der USB-Anschlüsse externe Speicher hinzufügen. An der Unterseite lässt dich der MiniPC jedenfalls aufschrauben und dadurch die Erweiterungen einbauen.

Der Lieferumfang ist ebenfalls zu benennen, da ein kleines Täschchen mitgeliefert wird. Dazu ein HDMI-Kabel, das Stromgerät, eine Befestigungsplatte, wenn man den MiniPC irgendwo anbringen möchte und Schrauben. Ich habe den MiniPC während einer Aktion gekauft und so bekam ich die graumelierte originale Geekom-Tasche dazu, die auch etwas her macht und den Transport noch sicherer gestalten lässt.

Zusammenfassend kann ich sagen, dass ich ein richtiger Fan von dem MiniPC und von Geekom geworden bin und ich die Firma definitiv weiter im Auge behalten werden. Der MiniPC hat sich schon jetzt gelohnt und bereitet mir sehr viel Freude. Er verbindet in meinen Augen hohe Leistungsperformance mit geringer Größe und das ist etwas, bei dem ich dachte, dass man lange danach suchen müsste. Die vorab verbauten Speicher (RAM und SSD) sind Markenprodukte, was mich positiv überrascht und ein Zeichen davon sind, dass jemand bei der Entwicklung und Ausstattung mitgedacht hatte. Die (leichte) Erweiterbarkeit finde ich gut und werde ich nach und nach angehen und freue mich schon darauf, aus dem Ding sowohl meinen Arbeits- und Alltagsrechner als auch mein Media Server zu machen und somit mehrere Dinge in einem vereint haben zu können. Das vorinstallierte Windows 11 Pro ist ebenfalls eine Überraschung, da man sonst nur die Home Edition bekommt. Somit kann ich diesen MiniPC weiterempfehlen und hoffe, dass Geekom weiter daran arbeitet dieses Niveau zu halten und sogar auszubauen. Ich bin auf die zukünftigen Produktentwicklungen in diesem Bereich gespannt.

text:
(I'm editing my review because I thought the voltage reading I was getting on the CPU seemed high but I have confirmed with an Intel rep that it is within the normal range for the CPU in this machine.)

I payed $190 CDN for this computer in December of 2022. Performance is quite good considering it has a 15W TDP processor in it. I have upgraded the RAM to 16GB from the original 8GB and I have added a 500GB 2.5" SSD in addition to the original 128GB SSD.

Pros: Good performance for the price and power draw. Can run many low end or older games quite decently. I had decent experiences running overwatch 2, Fallout New Vegas, Half LIfe 2, Portal 2, Half Life, Half Life Infinite, Golf with Friends, and other older games at 720P with low or medium settings. Overwatch 2 was a bit stuttery on occasion but doubling the RAM to 16GB seems to have smoothed it out. The machine also has many great features, such as: Socketed RAM that can be swapped out. An M2 SATA SSD (stock config) that can be swapped out and upgraded. It also has an available pre-wired 2.5" drive bay so you can easily install a 2.5" SSD. The bottom of the computer is easily removed with four small screws and all the upgradable components are easily accessible immediately upon opening the computer. Also, the BIOS is surprisingly robust and open ended given that this is an OEM machine. You can TDP up the CPU if you're brave and have the computer in a cold room. You can change the amount of RAM to allocate to the integrated graphics, and you can tweak memory timings. Is the bios a pretty looking graphical interface? No, but it is a UEFI bios with a lot of options to play with. Also, the machine did not come with any bloatware that I was aware of. Just Windows and drivers. The windows 11 pro installation was activated. No missing drivers in device manager.

Cons: The machine gets to 70-80C under load in a 22C room which is what my home is usually heated to. By under load I mean running 2 high res videos on two seperate screens (which it does without any noticeable frame drops), or running a game, stuff like that. Obviously if you do a 30 minute cinebench marathon it's going to probably get warmer. Are these temperatures a problem? Absolutely not. However if you were to be in a very hot part of the world without air conditioning, and you were to run this computer in say a 35 celsius environment, I'd be watching the temperatures of the computer's processor more carefully. Having said that, the same is true of any machine with a small heatsink in hot environments, such as laptop computers or SFF computers, so that's not necessarily a con against this specific computer. The only real genuine con I've found with this machine is that the RAM is single channel (only one slot). Having said that, the only situation where that will matter for a machine in this class is the integrated graphics. Could I get a few more FPS in Fallout with dual channel RAM? Possibly. Is it a deal breaker? No. Also this computer runs Chrome OS Flex and Fyde OS (a fork of Chrome OS) flawlessly with zero issues. Also when I removed the included 8GB 2400Mhz RAM and replaced it with 16GBX1 2666Mhz RAM as well as adding a 500GB SATA SSD the machine booted up within about 10 seconds and posted immediately. It also correctly set the RAM speed to 2666Mhz. The SSD was immediately available in disk management as well as the BIOS.

Noticeable quirks based on my findings: possibly innaccurate vCore readings, definitely innacurate RAM speed readings (2666 RAM reads at 667 instead of 1333. It's definitely running at 2666 though). Also I was somewhat disappointed with the sound quality from the built in 3.5mm output and upgraded to a cheap and cheerful Soundblaster Play 3 external DAC dongle which sounds somewhat better while also offering more sound profile tweaks. Works well with this device.

Good value for money. Good cheap PC for a media center, or retro gaming, or maybe for your grandparents who want to surf the web and watch youtube videos. Also pretty decent for MS office which I have used on it. Competent basic every day PC at a low price.

A scan using the Intel Driver Assistant also did not show an update available for this driver. No amount of fiddling fixed this issue until I manually initiated a Windows update, which somehow found and installed a later version of the display audio driver (version 2020 instead of 2019). The PC is now back to normal with ~0% CPU at idle. The Windows update resulted in some bloatware installed which I had to manually delete, a small price to pay.
3. Playing AV1 encoded videos (resource intensive) with VLC reaches the limit of this Mini quickly. At 1080, play is smooth but at 1440, play is laggy as CPU touches 100 percent, and at 4K, play freezes or won't start. Interestingly, most of the difficult files (including 4k) will play nicely through the Chrome browser which might have a more efficient AV1 decoder in its built-in video player. Rare to see VLC (v 3.0.16) got beat.

Aside from the initial pain of configuring/customizing a new PC, specially to a 4K monitor, I found this Mini-PC to be quite adequate. It starts in 30 seconds, surfs the web quickly, with multiple tabs opened. It will play 4K video (H264 encoded) without a glitch using VLC and stream 1080 content quite happily. Overall, it behaves like a mid-level desktop and can serve as such with an external drive connected via USB. When used with a 4K monitor/TV, the 4K display output produces stunning images/video with lots of detail and texture, great for photo editing work. Recommended.
I gave this 5 stars but had wished Beelink would be more thorough in checking driver compatibility first before release (to save me some grief).

text:
This is a great little PC in a small package, but takes a bit of tweaking to get it running properly.

PROs:
Great small form factor PC, nice build quality and small footprint. Once configured correctly, it runs like a dream with my 3 screens - 2 x 32" Samsungs and 1 x 24" LG in portrait mode. I have not used it for gaming, but for streaming and dev work it runs amazingly well - no lag or difference from my old i7-13900k gaming machine. The file transfer speeds are insanely fast, and I have several USB hubs with many peripherals running without any issues. All in all, it's mindblowing how much computing power is in such a small box.

CONs:
There is a decent amount of configuration required to get it running seamlessly.

First of all, the included HDMI cable would not connect to some of my displays, and the HDMI ports are fickle depending on the cables you are using. I ended up buying JSAUX and oldboytech cables from Amazon and I can confirm that both of those brands work, but several others I tried did not.

Secondly, the default fan noise is really loud, even when it isn't under load. I had to go to the Geekom website and download a BIOS unlocker so that I could enter the BIOS and turn the thermal profile to quiet.

Lastly, the out-of-the-box drivers are out of date and need updating in order to get things working properly. I use three screens and could not get them all to connect at the right resolution until I downloaded the latest Intel Arc drivers from Intel. Similarly with the wireless and bluetooth, they were finicky until I downloaded and installed the latest drivers.

Conclusion:
Don't get me wrong, this is a great little box, but it is not plug-and-play if you have specific setup requirements. That said, I would happily buy it again knowing what I know now, but it is the reason why it doesn't get a 5 star from me. I spent a good few hours of trial and error to get it running how I like it, but now I am very happy with it.

text:
GMKTec EVO-T1: A Mini-PC Worthy of Your Family’s AI-Learning Journey?

Is the GMKTec EVO-T1 an excellent choice for your school age children (grandchildren) to learn and build a solid foundation in AI tools while being capable of supporting more advanced AI development and experimentation as their interest and skills grow?
As a Grandparent who attended High School during the early days of the development of Personal Computing, I know firsthand how valuable it can be to have easy access to technology tools to experience, learn and experiment with developing technologies. Having access to these tools can provide a lifelong knowledge base that could lead to meaningful opportunities. Developing a solid technology skill base today is even more important than when I was a student. AI technology development is progressing so much more rapidly than in the past that I fear that if my grandchildren do not get on the learning train early, they might find themselves left shut out of future opportunities and find that catching up to their peers is an impossible task. One of the most satisfying and impactful gifts I can give them is the tools and opportunity today to learn skills that they can call upon to succeed in the future.
This was the basis for my purchase of the GMKtec EVO-T1. No doubt with its technology leading Intel Core Ultra 9 285H CPU and ARC 140T iGPU, it can easily handle any computing task that my family could ask it to do. The capability to upgrade the RAM from the included 64 MB to 128 MB and outfit it with up to three M2 NVME storage drives allows for future expansion. I was also impressed with the array of IO options available such as Audio ports front and back, dual 2.5 GB Lan ports and an Oculink port to support adding a separate GPU card to either support the needs of demanding game play or more demanding AI computation models and tools.
This level of hardware should allow the GMKTec EVO-T1 to function in almost any other technology roll such as a Home Server, Router or NAS long after my Grandchildren have outgrown and moved past its role as an AI learning and development platform. The attractive and compact design ensures it fits easily into a home office or workspace and with its cooling capabilities it does not create a noisy environment that might distract or take away from an effective learning environment.
I want to provide a capable technology device for my family to learn and develop AI skills beyond those provided by built in Internet connected LLM models offered to most computer user. I selected the GMKtec EVO-T1 believing it is up to this task and more. I want it to fill the gap between those that are highly advanced with AI development and require high end multi-GPU hardware in a dedicated AI Lab and what is currently available to novice AI users as part of most consumer computing hardware and software. At the same I wanted it to provide the added security and privacy of local AI usage thus removing the need to be tied to the public internet or to subscription fee models.

Here is my assessment of how well the GMKtec EVO-T1 meets my needs and hopefully it will be of use in your purchasing decision.

Most basic AI tasks start with using LLM’s through text-based prompts to have the AI models provide some answer to the prompt. To allow for easier access to these models several AI GUI wrapper applications are available. I tested the following AI GUI applications with several of the same prompts on the GMKtec EVO-T1 to ensure operations and determine if there were any issues. All these AI Wrappers perform their function and which one you choose as your daily driver will be an individual choice. I have included some brief notes beside each one based upon my impressions.

AIPC
This is the default application provided on the desktop. It has several advanced capabilities beyond simple prompt-based queries and provides them in a logical structure such as document analysis, translation, meeting minutes and image retrieval all accessed under the Skills menu. It also provides a LLM Model/App Store tab which allows access to eight popular LLM’s models locally along with the ability to also access many more paid Internet connected models and tools. You can use the AIPC application completely locally by simply clicking the “Offline Mode” selection on the screen following application launch. Or if you wish to utilize the Internet AI capabilities then on the launch screen you enter your email address and click on the “Send Code” button. Following receiving the code you enter it in the “Verification Code” field, check the User Agreement box and click “Login.”
I found this application to be feature rich and convenient for most normal AI interactions along with providing several more advanced capabilities that might be of use. From my inquiries the GMKtec team authorizes and approves the addition of any LLM’s that are provided on the local selection to ensure security and useability. Given that this application is new it is still evolving, and documentation and screens are not yet polished for an English audience. Given the ease of use of the application for a wide audience I am sure any improvements will arrive in short order.
LM Studio, JAN & AI Playground for Intel ARC
All these GUI wrappers provide basic functionality and additional features that might be useful. I have listed these together because when tested they all fully utilized the GMKtec EVO_T1 Intel Arc 140T iGPU. One caveat is that many other tools natively support the Nvidia GPU. Therefore, they require some more advanced configurations to allow us to utilize the iGPU instead of only the CPU. While my testing shows the Core Ultra 9 285H CPU does a respectable job while executing AI LLM functions it does not perform this task as fast and as effectively as the Intel ARC 140T iGPU. If speed of execution is desired, then you would want to investigate advanced configurations by searching PyTorch and ipex.llm and learning how to configure those within the other AI GUI wrapper applications.
LM Studio allows for almost any Open Source LLM model to be downloaded for local use and provides a well-integrated API back end as well as RAG integration. JAN provides one of the easiest GUI to navigate and use and also provides an API. While AI Playground for Intel ARC provides full and deep utilization of the Intel libraries and iGPU hardware. This allows for the use of CPU, NPU or iGPU selection while providing some preconfigured tools to accomplish image enhancement, text to image and text to video AI Generation within this GUI. A nice capability for the user.

GPT4All, Ollama, OpenWebUI, Msty, Cherry Studio, Anything LLM
I found that these tools utilize the Intel CPU and do not support the Intel ARC iGPU natively out of the box. My earlier comment that additional configurations work is needed to allow for iGPU use applies. I have confidence that some if not all these models will provide native use of the Intel iGPU in future releases and thus expand options for local model use.

So, what might be expected for Tokens/second results for local models run on the GMKtec EVO-T1 and what are its real-world functional capabilities? To answer this question, I ran samples in each of the following Generative AI functional areas. AI LLM Chat, Text to Image, Text to Video and AI Agents. AI LLM Chat was tested with a variety of prompts including plain text, document analysis, and coding. In each case my results only represent the average Tokens/sec not the quality of the output. From this data a few conclusions on the performance of the GMKTec EVO-T1 can be made. Each model was tested with the CPU and the iGPU as the main AI computational device as shown in the results.

Mistralv03:7b - CPU 9.95 T/s GPU 17.4 T/s
MINICPM-V - CPU 5.9 T/s GPU 9.8 T/s
QWQ:32b Q4 KM - CPU 2.7 T/s GPU 3.6 T/s
LLAMA3.1 :8b - CPU 11.8 T/s GPU 13.6 T/s
QWEN2.5:14b - CPU 6.2 T/s GPU 7.2 T/s
QWEN2.5:7b - CPU 10.6 T/s GPU 14.3 T/s
QWEN3-coder:30b - CPU 9.2 T/s GPU 19.1 T/s
DEEPSEEK_R1 :32b - CPU 2.8 T/s GPU 3.5 T/s
DEEPSEEK_R1 :14b - CPU 5.3 T/s GPU 7.9
DEEPSEEK_R1:8b - CPU 10.2 T/s GPU 15.6 T/s
GPT-OSS:20b - CPU 11.8 T/s GPU 15.5
In evaluating these results, I personally use the benchmark of my reading speed ability. Meaning that if I am waiting for text to display while reading then performance seems slow, and this would not be an effective use of my time. This benchmark will vary by person, but I find for me anything around 4-6 T/s is a comfortable reading speed to ensure understanding. Hence some of the 32b models when utilizing the iGPU are close to meeting this benchmark and I would find them useful when being executed on the EVO-T1.

For text to image and text to video several tools were used but primarily Comfy.UI. In all testing cases results with image generation finished in a reasonable time of less than a minute but with video generation this time expanded considerably depending upon settings. I find this functionality to be useable for learning and basic tasks on the EVO-T1. If video generation needs are higher for speed and resolution, then it is comforting to know that the EVO-T1 provides for this and other more demanding VRAM capabilities by including an Oculink port so that a separate and much more powerful GPU can be installed and utilized. Unfortunately, I do not have a more powerful GPU available, so this capability was not tested.

To examine the GMKtec EVO-T1 performance with the execution of AI Agents I utilized n8n installed in a Docker Container on the Windows 11 operating system. Instructions are easily available to accomplish this and were easy to follow with the installation and operation going seamlessly. Several simple to complicated AI Agents were tested with workflows utilizing many node types calling both local and Internet LLM’s, Websites, API, and Data Bases. The GMKtec EVO-T1 with its powerful Core Ultra 9 285H CPU and 64 MB of RAM ensured that all steps and function worked quickly and flawlessly. I ordered up 14 of these units (a couple different orders) and started installing them in client locations. Within a week, we started getting calls about the units trying to boot from PXE or saying "Operating System not found." Thought it was a fluke at first but eventually determined that this company has their own white-labeled M.2/PCIe SSDs and this series of Optiplex 7010s do NOT like them. In the end, we ended up having to replace the half dozen or so units we couldn't really swap out with new, brand-name SSDs to resolve the problem.

We did manage to return 7 of them, but I had to go buy big boxes as we'd already tossed the ones they were delivered in. Then we had to hound Amazon for several days to get the seller to actually refund the money (several days in, two of them had been refunded, but Amazon's site just kept saying "Refund in process" and they'd refund the money once they all were received). After a few pokes at Amazon, we did get our money back, but man did this cost me a lot of man hours having to rebuild failed/incompatible SSDs on the fly.

I don't know what's wrong with their white-labeled SSDs, but they must be incredibly cheap (and modern Optiplex units only really like NVMe models that can run in native RAID mode).

For the record, I did go to their web site and it looks like it was done in Microsoft Word. I managed to get a request out explaining my situation but only got a "please create a ticket" response.

I'd used OEMGENUINE in the past with good results, but wow was this a disaster. Do NOT buy these units unless you intend to put a quality SSD in it!!

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
Mine arrived in excellent packaging with a generic wired keyboard, mouse, and USB 2.0 "n" network dongle. It didn't have the internal wireless system. Not ideal but works just fine.

There was some damage to the finish on the housing at the back where it wasn't noticeable. It was covered up with some black permanent marker. Also, at this price point, not unexpected for a refurbished item.

I'm using mine as a media station at my 4K TV. I was disappointed at how noisy the fan was but went into the power settings and found that limiting CPU to 70% and changing cooling scheme from Active to Passive in the Windows power settings makes it effectively silent. Even at 70% it has way more CPU performance than the laptop it replaced and has no problem processing video at 4k and the cheap WiFi works just fine for streaming 4k video. The HDMI passes audio through my TV to my 5.1 receiver just fine making for fantastic sound.

Paired with an Air Mouse remote control https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0DXFPSSSK it's just about perfect for a home media and internet surfing setup. I went from 3 remotes with my Roku to just 1 and ditched the ads while gaining the ability to surf in a real browser.

It uses a SATA SSD and has a free M.2 SSD slot and a free M.2 WiFi slot if you wanted to upgrade or ditch the dongle and use something more modern with an external antenna. I get full bars and it's plenty of storage for me, so I probably won't bother with upgrading anything.

Over-all I'm extremely happy with my purchase. If it were more expensive, I might knock it down to 4 stars, but for this price you can't ask for much more.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
For those considering this machine, please read carefully. I selected a reseller with a price higher than the lowest offered. Why? Because at the time of my selection, the lowest price seller had 71% satisfaction rating, but for $6 more I selected another seller with a 90% satisfaction rating (TekRefurbs.com). This is especially important with a renewed computer! Many reviews reflect problems due to the differences in resellers, so it pays to select carefully.

The first thing I did on receiving the computer was open the case and remove the new 256 GB ssd, and install a 1 TB nvme ssd into the m.2 socket, and a 2 TB ssd into the hard drive caddy and reinstalled the caddy and closed the case. The computer was spotless inside and out. The next step is very important. I went to the Dell website and downloaded the BIOS update. I run linux on a multi boot system, but linux cannot install the new bios so I booted into windows for the bios update. Just follow the on screen instructions and the update takes just a few minutes. It is crucial to update the bios as the machine is vulnerable until it is done. The machcine is capable of running Windows 11, but apparently the Windows 10 Pro that comes with the computer will not allow updating. Since I did not install Windows 10, but moved my existing drives into the computer, I was all set with Windows 11. Many users prefer Windows 10.

I recommend before buying or receiving the computer that the user/owner manual in pdf format be downloaded from the dell site as it is really mandatory if you are going to get your newly renewed machine set up properly. Curiously this computer will run with either the 65 watt or the 130 watt power supply cord; mine came with the 65 watt power supply and it works flawlessy. There are also two other m.2 sockets on the motherboard for WLAN and WWAN cards as shown in the manual for those who want or need them. The cards and cables and antenna are available on Amazon.

I hope this information is useful to any who take time to read it. The machines are not for gamers as they do not have the graphics horsepower for that use, but are great for other applications if you choose the reseller carefully. It is a shame the machines suffer less than stellar ratings due to the disparities between reseller preparations. Choose wisely and you will be rewarded.

text:
The Short Version: (Please skip this as it has spoilers if you prefer to read ‘The Long Version’.)
16 GB RAM, 1 TB M.2 SSD. I noticed a vibration from the CPU fan and contacted TekRefurbs and they are shipping me a new fan. Their response time was quick and they were eager to make sure I was a satisfied customer. I added 16 GB more RAM, a 2.5 inch SSD, a low-profile graphics card (supports up to 3 monitors), and a dual M.2 card along with 2 more M.2 SSDs. With the 2 DP ports and HDMI port on the motherboard, I ACTUALLY RAN 6 MONITORS (all at once) while streaming 6 different videos on YouTube. I picked this up to replace my DELL Optiplex 9020 which is too old for Windows 11. (As of now, Microsoft has stated that they will be ending their support for Win 10 by the end of 2024.) Running Crystal Disk Mark I got transfer rates of 1.7 GBps (read) and 1.1 GBps (write) on the SSD that came with the computer and 2 GBps (read) and 1.6 GBps (write) on the HP M.2 SSD I added. **UPDATE: I replaced one of my M.2 SSDs with a fanxiang S660 4TB PCIe 4.0 NVMe M.2 SSD and now get the following speeds (read) 3.5 GBps and (write) 3.1 GBps. They actually make faster M.2s but they far exceed the capability of the motherboard.

I’m thrilled with both the computer and customer service couldn’t be happier with this purchase.

The Long Version:
I have purchased over 1,000 items from Amazon over the past decade and I only give reviews on the best (or the worst) items I have ordered. The renewed DELL Optiplex 7060 SFF I got from TekRefurbs is amazing and so is their customer support. (I had a little vibration with the CPU fan and I sent them a message about it, they replied the next business day and offered to send a replacement.) Awesome service!

With Microsoft stating that they will be ending their support for Windows 10 towards the end of 2024, I decided to replace my Optiplex 9020 SFF (not Win 11 compatible) now, rather than wait for a possible shortage of affordable/renewed Win 11 computers in the future. (As of now, the vast majority of people are still running Win 10.)

The model that I got was the 16 GB/ 1 TB version (other variants may be sold by different vendors). When I opened the box (and even the case) it looked like it was brand new, I couldn’t find even the smallest amount of dust anywhere. Included with the desktop was a free wireless mouse & keyboard and a few BT & WiFi dongles in addition to the built-in features from the motherboard itself. (Even without the dongles, I still have BT & WiFi connectivity.) **Models sold by TekRefurbs come with the built-in M.2 WiFi card which supports both 5 & 2.4 Ghz but for the fun of it I replaced it with the AX210 WiFi 6E Card M.2 NGFF and connected it to the 2 internal antennas.

Display Support: While some desktops (from other sellers) only have 2 Display Ports (DP) and either a VGA port (or missing the 3rd port), mine came with 2 DPs and an HDMI port. (Nice touch!) While being able to connect to 3 monitors (off of the motherboard) is nice, I added an inexpensive VisionTek Products Radeon 6350 SFF 1GB DDR3 3M DMS59 with 2X DVI-I to VGA Adapter Graphics Card that adds support for an additional 3 monitors AND I RAN A TOTAL OF 6 MONITORS AT ONCE while streaming different videos on each monitor. Granted, I’m not a gamer so I’m not concerned with Frames Per Second (FPS) but it did actually work (I normally just run 3 monitors stacked vertically – one on top of each other).

Storage Capacity (hard drives): This model, like most of the DELL SFF cases have 3 SATA ports and the newer models have a space for an M.2 SSD. The model I purchased came with a 1 GB M.2 SSD and the DVD drive and the cables were provided to connect a second hard drive as well. There is room for a 3.5 inch hard drive or you can get an adapter to mount the smaller 2.5 inch drive if you wish (there are adapters that can hold up to three 2.5 inch drives in a single 3.5 inch slot). But why settle for just one additional hard drive when you can have a total of FOUR HARD DRIVES? Thanks to the Dual M.2 PCIE Adapter for SATA or PCIE NVMe SSD with Advanced Heat Sink Solution,M.2 SSD NVME (m Key) and SATA (b Key) 22110 2280 2260 2242 2230 to PCI-e x 4 Host Controller Expansion Card, you can have up to 3 M.2 SSDs plus one 2.5 inch SSD. ***You can also get the M.2 NVME to PCIe 3.0 x4 Adapter with Aluminum Heatsink Solution (single M.2 slot) and add up to two additional 2.5 inch SSDs. I actually recommend getting this card instead of the one I purchased because the second M.2 slot has to connect to one of the SATA ports from the motherboard so the transfer speed is the same as if you connected a 2.5 inch SSD (which are cheaper). Running Crystal Disk Mark I got transfer rates of 1.7 GBps (read) and 1.1 GBps (write) on the M.2 SSD that came with the computer and 2 GBps (read) and 1.6 GBps (write) on the HP M.2 SSD I added.

RAM: The model I purchased came with 16 GB RAM (two 8 GB chips) which was nice because I added an additional 16 GB RAM for a small price. (32 GB is more than enough RAM for most applications.)

Free Extras: The extra dongles, mouse and keyboard are nice touches and pretty good quality as well. I admit that I haven’t tested them because I used a lighted keyboard (wired) and Logitech Trackball.

Summary: Whether you are using the computer ‘as is’ or you want to upgrade it, this is an excellent choice for an affordable and (still) powerful system that will carry you through the Windows 11 lifespan (and probably beyond). Despite this being the Small Form Factor (SFF) model, there is room to add a (low profile) graphics card, USB-C 3.2 card, M.2 card or whatever you wish. (Just be mindful of the power requirements of the graphics cards - this comes with a 200 watt power supply.)

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
NOTE: When I ordered this PC on 12/4/2022 it came from Skytech USA.

PROS:
1. Excellent condition - looks brand new. Couldn't find any scratches or defects. No dust or dirt visible inside or out.
2. As you can see from the pics, all the specs matched what was advertised.
3. Comes with boxed, basic keyboard and 2-button corded mouse. Full-sized keys & layout with a numeric keypad in a smaller-than-standard frame (17x5"). Has a soft, non-'clicky' tactile feel, and is mostly quiet with a little bit of key rattle.
4. On initial power up, you start with the standard Windows 10 setup of picking your region, keyboard, etc, so it was a fresh Windows install. No issues with activation.
5. Time from Dell logo appearing on screen to Windows desktop is about 10 seconds. Not too bad!
6. Very quiet. Even up close I can barely hear the fan - tho I've only run PVR software on it so far.
7. No bloatware. The only installed non-standard software was VLC Media Player.
8. Tool-less hardware mounting provides easy access to memory slots, swapping out storage devices, etc.

CONS:
1. Would have preferred a single 8GB RAM module vs the 2x4GB config it came with that uses up both slots. If you want to expand the memory you'll have to discard one or more of the existing modules.
2. Question the SATA SSD. I realize the object is to cut costs to the max, but for under 24 bucks you could install a same-sized, more reputable-brand M.2 NVMe drive for better performance, and free up the lone drive bay to boot. Makes one wonder just how cheap (reliable?) the included KingFast SSD is.

OTHER:
1. Cannot be upgraded to Windows 11. This may be a pro or con pending your viewpoint.
2. No wi-fi dongle or card included. Only network/internet connection is via ethernet cable. Not a deal breaker - dongles are cheap if you need wi-fi.
3. Installing an external graphic card could be problematic, unless it's low-power, half-height, and VERY thin. There's less than an inch of space between the slot and the side of the power supply (see pic). Plus, the PC's power supply is only 180 watts.
4. There are rubber feet on both the bottom and along the left side, so you can stand it vertical like a tower if desired.
5. RAM and M.2 slots are under the drive bay.
6. SHOULD you want to install a 3.5 HDD, the only full-size drive bay is filled with a caddy holding the SATA SSD. The caddy snaps out, but you'll have purchase a separate 3.5 caddy for your HDD as there is no inherent way to mount anything directly into the bay. Everything requires some manner of snap-in caddy.

The cons you kind of expect with this kind of product, so overall I give it 5 stars. I would not use it for high-end gaming. Don't know of a powerful enough half-height graphic card that would fit in the slot, but for non graphic-intensive tasks and some older games, this should work very well. So far, very happy with the purchase.

Missing Bluetooth: The product specifications stated that a USB Bluetooth adapter was included. The package I received had no Bluetooth adapter at all, another failure to provide the advertised equipment.

Broken Keyboard: To make matters worse, the included keyboard arrived broken. Both of the plastic tilt legs were snapped off, showing a complete lack of quality control before shipping.

Receiving a product with the wrong CPU, missing components, and broken accessories is unacceptable. Buyers should be extremely cautious, as the product description is not a reliable indicator of what you will actually receive.

text:
I ordered 3 of these. On paper, they are great. The first one I received had a 256GB SSD instead of the advertised 512. It also only had 8GB memory instead of the 16GB advertised. I contacted amazon support and they wanted me to contact the seller. I contacted the seller and they said "We are sorry for the inconvenience. Please reach out to Amazon customer support for a return/replacement as this was fulfilled by Amazon." According to Amazon "Sorry, this order is not eligible for a refund under the A-to-z Guarantee because you have not yet submitted a return request with the seller. Please request a return via the Online Returns Center and allow the seller two days to get back to you."

I had already remotely deployed the unit in a customer's environment, installed AV, Office, & joined to their domain and setup user profiles, so I just gave up.

The other two, came as advertised, but the 2nd unit I setup is so slow it took about 2 hours to get through the out of box experience. Once in windows, it was not possible to open an explorer window or browser. the cursor just spun for hours. I tried about 10 times after rebooting, etc. I gave up on that one as well ready to return it. (haven't tried starting that process again)

I was able to setup the 3rd unit in place of the 2nd one okay, but later I noticed it wasn't as quick as it should be for a computer with a 6 core i5, 16GB of ram and SSD. Task manager showed it running at .79GHz. So I changed the performance profile to High Performance and rebooted. That changed nothing. I created my own custom high performance profile, selected that and rebooted. Again only .79GHz. I checked the advanced power settings and min and max CPU were set to 100%. I then reset the bios to factory defaults and low and behold on boot I got a message that the type of power supply could not be determined. When this happens to a DELL, it throttles the CPU at the slowest possible speed. The seller is providing a PSU that on paper would have more than enough power for this micro pc, but the barrel jack is too long so the center pin doesn't make contact. That is required for the system to determine the wattage of the PSU.

THE SELLER INTENTIONALLY TURNED OFF THE POST ADAPTER WARNING about the PSU not being identified. I verified this to be the case on ALL 3 UNITS! Unfortunately, I don't have time to wait for returns and refunds, so I ordered myself 2 new PSU's that are advertised as being for this specific model. I will be returning the 2nd unit because despite the PSU .79GHz issue, there has got to be something else going on with the hardware as the other two units were still somewhat usable at .79GHz. If you don't believe me look at the images.

Update 1/2/2022:
After ordering 7 of these, I can say that I've received only 1 unit with the advertised Wireless KB & Mouse. Sadly only the mouse worked...

text:
I honestly don’t know what I was expecting with this speaker. To be honest, all the reviews said that it was a good speaker for using with Zoom and teams, etc. hinting to the fact that it was probably more for business than anything else.
I will start by saying that this speaker looks good in person. It feels hefty, well built, and it has a decent length cable with both USBA and USB-C connectors, which is always a plus. I also like the touch controls on the surface of the speaker.
Installation was dead, simple, just plugged it into my Mac, and it instantly recognized it. The sound quality when watching YouTube videos is decent, obviously good, but not great considering the size of the speaker. So for my needs, it gets the job done.
The only downside and the reason why I am not giving it five stars is that for some reason the notifications for my Mac don’t come through the speaker very well. On the Mac sound control panel you have two different volumes: the volume for the audio, and then above that another slider for the notifications volume. And while the volume for actual content is only about halfway, the volume for notifications has to be all the way to 100% and even then they sound tinny. My solution to this has been to push my notifications through the speakers on my monitor, which while admittedly, not great are more powerful and so I can get my notifications to be more loud that way. Not an elegant solution, but it works for me. It’s a shame because otherwise it’s a great little speaker. If you keep your expectations in check for what it is. As for the value for money, I was ready to give it high marks, but given the problem mentioned above with notifications, I unfortunately cannot say that it’s a great value, because I am sure that some people will say that for the price of $74 and given its small size it should do everything well (I bought a similar speaker from another brand for work for $24 that does exactly the same job as this one just add us a slightly lower sound quality, so for $50 more this speaker should have that other one be in every department and unfortunately it doesn’t.). But if you’re willing to live with that small inconvenience, it’s not a bad little speaker.

I got this new a couple of years ago, to replace a terribly old Mac that couldn't keep up anymore. I've been astonished at how fast this little PC has been. The specs don't really tell you the whole story. The folks at HP managed to optimize this machine so that it's just blazing fast compared to other computers I've had that were closer to top of the line in their day. It may not hold up well for instensive things like video procesing or bulk graphic editing in Illustrator, but for the vast majority of productivity type tasks, this tiny PC is perfect. You'd never know you're on a mini PC except the fact that it's stone cold quiet and doesn't have great HD space (just get a 500GB flash drive, they're cheap). With 7 USB ports and a 2 DisplayPorts, even the lack of HDMI isn't a very big deal. Thunderbolt would be nice but there are workarounds. I've got this thing hooked into a 43 inch 4K monitor and everything looks beautiful. Mouse is a bit slower on the big screen, but that's it.

Upgrading to Win 11 was as easy as upgrading the TPM to 2.0 w/ HPs official tool, and using MSFT's registry override published on their site with instructions how to install Windows 11 on machines deemed incapable (Windows will tell you the CPU on this machine isn't up to par, but that's ridiculous). Then during the ISO ugprade you need to selected advanced and turn automatic updates during installation OFF or the install will cut out. Also, all the warnings about how if you upgrade on a machine deemed incapable will make you ineligible for future Windows updates are totally bogus - updates work fine. Windows 11 is way better than 10, especially for multiple monitors. I ran the Performance Monitor app in Windows 11, and not only did this machine pass with flying colors, it scored an 8.7 in the CPU area - where 5 is a passing score. So not only can the CPU handle Windows 11, it handles it a lot better than plenty of the machines deemed capable of Win 11.

Buying one of these for $110 refurbished for office, home, or school is a no brainer.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
As an I.T. professional for decades... I've opened a LOT of monitors. Yes, this does what you'd expect from a product perspective. I've ordered and installed a couple dozen of these so far. Great screens, no dead pixels, 27" with 2K resolution, comes with HDMI cable, built in power supply so no dumb wall wart or AC adapter. All good things... But let me tell you what the biggest perk is of this thing if you are buying a lot of monitors... THE PACKAGING.

Yes folks, you heard it here first. I appreciate SO MUCH the choices here. Dell nailed it:
- No styrofoam blocks that inevitably break in transit and then leave dozens of single pellets of static electricity annoyance that cling to everything like a toddler to a mom's leg when all she wants is to use the bathroom in peace
- No sliding a block of goods out of a too-tight box that won't move because the "handle" punch-ins were used and now they block any possible extraction of the contents of said box
- No stickers on the bezel that advertise stats about the monitor that you already purchased and don't need to have as selling points, but inevitably leave some sticky residue when removed
- No fingerprint magnet piano black covered in cellophane peels that you will either miss removing or you will remove and then will stick to you despite you flicking your wrist towards the trash can 8 times only to find it on your shoe later in the day
- No plastic sheet covering the screen taped on with industrial strength shipping adhesive tape with fiber reinforcements that surely will not pull off cleanly and will instead peel like a banana when you try to remove it
- No tape sealing every possible ingress point of the box that requires you to cut every seam wondering where the heck the open end is

They NAILED it. The box is opened by laying it on its side, cutting a single piece of tape, opening the lid, pulling out the power and HDMI cables, stand parts (assembled tool-less), and then lifting off a single cardboard insert to reveal a foam bag which is pre-torn at the middle-bottom and you can tear further to expose the VESA mount and snap the stand into the monitor, lift it up and out... plug in cables, snap on a cover, and done.

You are left with only cardboard save for a few sheets of paper, a foam bag, and a plastic bag from the power cable (not sure why a bag is needed) and a plastic wrap (that easily slides off) from the HDMI cable.

If you need quick turnaround and/or appreciate relatively friendly environmentally conscious packaging, this is the winner. Best I've ever seen in terms of packaging.

Plus it looks nice as a white monitor. Well worth the price if you can find it sub $200. Even at full price it's worth it if you are buying in bulk as it will save you time and hassle in deployment. Well done Dell! I bought one... then dozens more. It's now my "go-to" monitor for office use.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
Gosh, where to even begin? I've been using Dell Monitors for over a decade now - regardless of what brand PC system I was using. I've always found Dell monitors to be a cut above, given what you spend.

Over the past week, one of the audio components that I had on a shelf directly above my previous Dell monitor, fell from the shelf, hit the table and bounced back into my Dell screen, smashing it - talk about a negative surprise. So I had to find a PC monitor quickly to replace it. Problem is that I needed a monitor whose height adjustment capabilities were a step above. So I called Dell, talked to a sales agent, who asked me what exactly I was looking for. I told him that my PC monitor needed to have substantial height (lowering and raising the monitor) capabilities.

After researching a variety of PC monitors, he recommended that I try the Dell S2425HS monitor, which had a height adjustment capability of 5"-6", which is phenomenal. You see, my monitor is sitting within a small nook space (height-wise), and I needed to have a monitor that would allow me to lower the screen substantially to fit into this space.

So I thanked him and immediately ordered it on Amazon - and it arrived the very next day. When it arrived, I was gratified to see the same care and packing of the monitor that Dell had always provided. Assembly was quick, and I was then surprised to discover that there were two 5-watt speakers (I don't know the actual size of the speakers) integrated inside the monitor.

After connecting everything and subsequently doing a color calibration of this new S2425HS (I do lots of photography, and I need an accurate monitor to process digital photos), I was gratified to then witness a wonderful-looking screen. As an aside, I also am an audiophile that maintains a desktop, near-field audio system around my PC. The gear used includes names such as KEF, Adcom, NAD, SMSL, and more - all providing me with a glorious audio experience while working.

And believe it or not, the biggest surprise for me - besides the excellent screen qualities of this new S2425HS - was the sound of these two 5 watt built-in speakers. In the settings menu on the monitor, you have the options to tune the sound of the integrated speakers for Movie, Music, Standard, Sports, and a few other modes. So I set mine to music, fully expecting these two little speakers to sound tinny and compressed due to their small size.

But boy was I surprised. The speakers had a fuller-bodied sound with excellent separation and an almost holographic sound quality while listening to a variety of materials. It is a good 5 steps above the typical built-in tiny speakers you get with some other monitors. This came as a welcomed treat because I periodically like to give my audiophile amps and associated electronics a rest. In fact, I was watching a band perform on YouTube just a few minutes ago, and for a second, I thought I was listening through my KEF speakers. Of course, when the bass section was performing, I realized then that I was listening to the PC monitor speakers because let's face it, those tiny speakers were limited with what they could do.

So all in all, I am absolutely delighted with this quality-made Dell S2425HS monitor. It provides superb screen and picture qualities, and also gives you the bonus of including two small, yet highly competent speakers that provide excellent sound qualities, despite their small size.

Highly recommended!
