text:
Es primera vez que compro un monitor de la marca Acer, anteriormente tuve un BenQ de 22 pulgadas.
Por lo que aquí dejo mis observaciones de este producto para quien el sirva y sea de ayuda :)

Paquete:
- Está bien empacado, viene en una caja más grande que las dimensiones de la propia caja en la que llega el monitor.

Qué incluye:
- Trae un cable HDMI de 1 metro.
- Trae su base y su brazo de plástico con acabado de piano, éste punto no me gusta en lo absoluto, ese acabado completamente reflejante es en lo personal desagradable ya que con el tiempo, el transportar, desmontar o hacer algo con el monitor será un imán de huellas y/o rayones en la base incluido el brazo que sostiene el monitor, solo es mera cuestión de estética que yo tomo en cuenta, ya que comparándolo con el monitor que tuve anteriormente de BenQ no había dicho problema.

Envoltura:
- El monitor viene bien protegido por la nieve seca que lo proteje, de igual forma viene envuelto en una bolsa de plástico para prevenir rayones.
- A los bordes del monitor tiene también protección de plástico para que al colocarle la base tus dedos no toquen la pantalla y la manchen pero ojo, aquí muy imporante saber que esos plásticos en los bordes de la pantalla están muy adheridos por lo que hay que quitarlos con muchísimo cuidado y lentitud para que si los quitas con la pantalla encendida verás una marca debajo de lo que se va quitando de la cinta como si estuvieses tocandolo con un dedo, cosa que da miedo porque se ve como el liquido de la pantalla se va moviendo, no es nada permanente y solo ocurre en este proceso, pero mucho cuidado, debieron reducir la fuerza del adhesivo.
- Los cables vienen bien envueltos, instructivos incluidos.

Monitor:
- El propósito para el cual yo uso este monitor y el por qué lo consideré en mi compra es por lo siguiente.
> Tasa de refresco:
- Es una notable e innegable diferencia pasar (en mi caso por primera vez) de un monitor de 60Hz a uno de 100Hz, que son nativos, nada de overclock.
> Calidad de imagen:
- Estoy bastante contendo por la calidad de imagen que proporciona, colores y contraste bien definidos, bastante configurable en los ajustes del monitor, un punto positivo es que tiene una función llamada: "Supernitidez" que como su nombre lo dice mejora la nitidez en el texto y la imagen en general.
> Ghosting:
- Acer incluye una tecnología bajo su propio nombre "VRB" que significa "Visual Response Boost" para evitar el problema del comunmente conocido ghosting, honestamente no me gusta esta función ya que en lo personal siento que el efecto es el contrario, se nota presencia de ghosting y un brillo notablemente reducido al usarse, he conseguido la configuración más balanceada y es desactivando el VRB, configurando el Over Drive en normal, bajar el brillo a un 50%, pero esto último ya depende de cada quien.
> Color:
- El color configurarlo en Usuario, el tipo de panel es VA "Vertical Alignment", tiene buenos ángulos de visión horizontales pero en los verticales empieza a perder algo de color y contraste, aunque tampoco es que vaya a estarlo viendo desde arriba, pero viendolo de frente tiene muy buena calidad, con eso estoy encantado.
> Brillo:
- El brillo es bastante elevado a mi parecer, teniéndolo a un 20% de intensidad, sigo notando que aún sigue siendo bastante elevado, no es tan incómodo de noche pero un punto a su favor es que puedes activar el modo "Luz azul baja" para evitar la fatiga en la vista, aunque siempre es recomedable tener como mínimo un poco de luz de fondo para que tus ojos no se cansen tan rápido.
> Retroiluminación:
- Aquí no cabe duda que Acer hizo un excelente trabajo, en mi caso, al poner una imagen completamente en negro, como el color: "#000000", no noto en lo absoluto ni un poquito de fugas de luz, ni la más mínima, cosa que me ocurrió lo contrario con BenQ que tenía 3 fugas de luz, que se notaban en imágenes muy oscuras, aquí no hay problema de eso, lo siento de mejor calidad porque la iluminación es uniforme de esquina a esquina.
> Botones:
- Contamos con varios botones, el principal es un joystick que se usa para moverse a través de la interfaz después de ver unos atajos con los otros botones que tiene arriba del joystick, es cómodo de usar, solo es tenerle cuidado para no dañarlo pues de eso dependemos por completo para éste mérito, de igual forma se confirma pulsándolo, el botón de encendido es el primero de la parte superior, al principio a ciegas puedes perderte pero una vez que lo ubicas ya no hay problema, por este lado ninguna queja.
> Extras:
- Nos incluye AMD FreeSync, cosa que no puedo aprovechar porque hago uso de un Intel UHD que no es compatible claramente.
- Modo "supernitidez" para mejorar aún más la calidad y detalles en texto e imágenes.
- Como contra, no trae altavoces, ni los más básicos, haciendo que dependas de unos conectados directamente a tu computadora.
- Tiene 1 HDMI y 1 VGA, hubiese preferido 2 HDMI porque VGA casi no se usa pero pues es lo que tenemos.
- Contamos con 1MS de tiempo de respuesta, bastante positivo para el gaming.

Si eres un usuario muy exigente en cuanto al ghosting, no te lo recomendaría pues tiene una leve presencia del mismo en movimientos rápidos, con el tiempo ya ni te das cuenta, no le tomo tanta importancia porque logré encontrar el ajuste balanceado, así que es mínimo cuando ocurre, sin duda alguna es una excelente compra y la diferencia entre 100Hz que tiene este monitor y 120Hz que sería lo común, no hay mucha diferencia, se siente todo bastante fluido, nada de fugas de luz, nada de parpadeos por inestabilidad en la retroiluminación que es LED, excelente calidad y nitidez en general, buenos ángulos de visión, buen tiempo de respuesta, marcos bien delgados para una experiencia más immersiva, estoy encantado con mi compra y lo recomiendo ámpliamente, sino llegas a estar satisfecho, recuerda que siempre puedes devolverlo. Espero haberles sacado algunas dudas al respecto pues veo que en la página de Acer casi no hay nada de información acerca de este monitor, específicamente el Acer KC242Y HBI a 100Hz, por lo que si más adelante encuentro algo más que añadir, lo haré, pero por el momento ha sido todo, si lo compran, disfrútenlo mucho, vale la pena! :)

title: 3.0 out of 5 stars
text:
The Acer K2 (PS5) wireless gaming headset does what it is advertised to do. I use it with my PC laptop: Long battery life (about a week at 12 hours per day usage). Bluetooth and USB dongle wireless connectivity (I can go anywhere in my home and it stays connected). 3mm sub miniature jack for wired analog connection (cable included). USB-C jack (USB-A to USB-C cable included) for charging (about 4 hours, during which the headset cannot be used). Microphone 270 degree arm swivel arc to allow using the mic on either the left or right side. It all works

Wireless setup can be tricky. I initially paired it with my PC laptop for Bluetooth (fuzzy sounding voice announces "Bluetooth Connected"; it sounds like low fidelity 8 bit encoding), it shows up in Windows Sound Settings as "Speakers K2". I think an older version of Bluetooth is used. Stereo sound listening is available, but when the microphone is used, sound switches to mono and stays there for the rest of the listening session.

When I wanted to switch to using the wireless USB dongle, which is a little large, I had to Unpair the Bluetooth connection in Windows Sound Settings to get my PC to stop trying to pair with it via Bluetooth, plug in the USB dongle, and restart my computer. When the USB Dongle successfully connects, a blinking blue LED on the dongle changes to steadily lit, and the 8 bit encoded fuzzy voice announces "USB Connected". With this connection method, stereo sound is maintained, even when the microphone is used. This is most important for gaming.

I give the headset a 3 star rating because, as other reviewers have stated, the sound quality is mediocre, far from being crisp, clear high fidelity. It sounds muffled. I had to use a free app from the Microsoft Store (FXSound) featuring a 9 stage audio equalizer, which somewhat improved the quality, making sound just barely passable.

Another app on the Microsoft Store works better (Boom3D) but it is "try before you buy". During its trial period (about 7 days), it provides full access to its features, including 19 stage equalizer (in Advanced mode) with surround and ambience settings. After the trial period expires, access to all features become locked, so I uninstalled it.

I chat a lot with friends in Discord. When I first used the microphone, I was told that my voice sounded muffled compared the the Logitech over-the-ear (uncomfortable) USB gaming headset I had been using.

If you are looking for a mostly comfortable, over-the-ear untethered headset for game sound, this one will work well, especially after getting used to audio quality. For $30 (US) I figure I got what I paid for.

text:
This worked at full USBv3 speed testing with a SSD. There was no difference in transfer speed when using this switch vs. plugging the USBv3 SSD straight to my computer. I was able to switch it between two computers easily using the button on the top of the box. (or remote operation, see below.)

Everything is "USB v3" in the A rectangular format (and all is labeled this way). Also included are two 2-foot USBv3 A to A cables. You will need extensions if your two computers are more than 4 feet apart!

But can it be used with USB-C? Yes, USB-C to A adapters DO work on these three USB-A ports (two sources/phones/computers, one peripheral device). NOTE - I did not test video or Thunderbolt through this - there are purpose made "KVM" switches with that capability I'd probably use instead. But "regular USB-C data devices like hard drives work fine" using physical cable adapters. I'd not expect anything more than USBv3 performance of course and didn't hook up to try anything faster.

The "power" input USB-C LOOKING connector on the switch box is a bit confusing, but if either of your source computers can supply a little bit of power, then you don't need to use the box's power USB-C port. (this is NOT a data USB-C port!) Instead, you can plug in the "remote switch cable" 4 foot long cable to this port. The button could sit by your keyboard and run to the switch behind the computer or back of desk, etc. The switch part is about 1" in diameter with an adhesive mounting disk included. This cable serves no other function - don't try to plug it into any OTHER USB-C port on anything!

There is a small manual. You won't need this - one side in Chinese and one in English covering both 4x1 and 2x1 switches. They don't even describe using the included remote switch for the 2x1 version (this article).

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I have an Asus Zenbook that's at least 7 years old (ancient by technology standards) and it has a very problematic USB hub. I love my laptop. It functions well except for the hub. I usually get OEM peripherals for my electronics. (I use PC and Android. I'm not a Mac/Apple user.)
In the case of the USB hub for my Zenbook the Asus replacement hub is garbage with a 1 star review on Asus website with warnings not to buy because of how fast it stops working. The Asus hub I purchased 3 months ago stopped working after using it 3 or 4 times. That's unacceptable in my opinion. I have tried other brands including Belkin, Anker and 2 others that I do not remember. None of them would deliver power to my laptop despite claiming they would. So I decided to try this hub. I need an external hub for the multiple USB ports because the Asus has no ports on the Zenbook itself, and power delivery (in a perfect world when everything works properly) should also be able to go thru the hub to charge the laptop. On my laptop, there's only one USB-C port to connect either direct power supply or a hub. You can't have both connected at the same time unless the hub allows power transfer to laptop, which the other brand hubs that I tried wouldn't support that power transfer, much to my frustration. This hub is the first hub that I've tried that will actually power my laptop. (I also switched my power supply cable to a Thunderbolt, so the combination of the new cable with this hub works.)
I use a wireless mouse with a dongle that needs to be plugged in. I have a digital voice recorder that plugs in directly via USB-A to transfer files to the laptop. I use SD cards in my camera and MP3 player that I need a hub to transfer that media onto the laptop. This hub will allow all of that. Every port works that I have tried on this Acer hub and this hub does the thing that the other hubs failed to do on my laptop. The power transfer was the big issue for me and this Acer hub solved the problem that several others including the OEM, Asus, failed to do. Because of how many months I have been dealing with the power supply problem, hubs not delivering what they promised and this being the only hub that did work, I rate this product at 5 stars. It's less expensive than the Asus hub that stops working immediately after purchasing. It has more ports than the Asus hub with the extra SD card reader that the Asus hub doesn't have. It's a heavier duty outer shell compared to the Asus. The cord is thicker and better protected compared to the Asus, so it reduces the chance for stressing or bending the cord in a way that could break the wires inside or break the connector away from the wires. It's just a better design overall, when compared to the Asus hub. I am extremely satisfied with this Acer hub and I would recommend it since it did the "impossible" task that no other brand could do for me. 5 stars, indeed.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
After years of juggling multiple laptops and WFH locations, I’m finally consolidating back to a single home office workspace. Despite that, the number of devices I work with has not changed. I realized I needed a better way.

I’m very happy with performance and look of the Minisopuru KVM. Searching online it seemed there were a large number of sub-$100 options, a mid-range centered around $200, and then high-end at $300+. As a tech professional, I’m leery of really inexpensive devices that seem to provide unrealistic performance for the cost, and many of them just really looked “cheap”. I also didn’t want to spend a fortune. This one is right in that middle range of price and performance, has a quality look, and functional design and layout.

Initially I was expecting a metal case as looks in pictures, but is actually a heavy and sturdy plastic, without any flex or feeling of a hollow enclosure. I’m using with a Dell desktop workstation and several Dell laptops running Windows and multiple Linux distros. The desktop stays plugged into the “PC1” connection, and laptops rotate as I need them via “PC2” connection. I’m not running dual monitors or 4K, but do have a QHD 2560x1440 Dell monitor, so can vouch for performance above FHD 1920x1080 resolutions. I’m not a gamer or high-end photo or video editor, so high refresh rates, low response times, video lag, color accuracy, or other performance indicators are not something I have experience with. However for normal desktop productivity and managing multiple systems and workspaces, the video performance appears indistinguishable from direct video connections.

I always feel I need more USB ports, even if I’m not using them ‘right now’. To leave the most flexibility, I connected one of the KVM 10Gbit USB-A ports to the USB3 hub built into the monitor, which I use for the USB keyboard connection, laptop cooler, fast-charging to a wireless charger, 3.5mm headphone/line audio out, and an open USB3 port. This leaves open a USB2, 10Gbit USB-A and USB-C ports, as well as another headphone connection on the KVM.

For setup, I felt was more efficient and a cleaner look if could orient the KVM vertically. I’ve collected a lot of wire mesh office products I use for both organization and airflow, and found a small mail/envelope divider was about the right size, and also provides channels for cable management...they’re also ideal for managing your workspace area laptop power supplies and cords.

This is my second Minisopuru product, and both have appeared as high quality builds, with good performance and support. I’ll check for their products again as have needs in the future.

text:
This is a very well-built KVM switch. The metal chassis feels solid, the included cables are excellent quality, and even the packaging deserves special praise. Everything connects easily, and switching between machines is absolutely instantaneous.

Unfortunately, there is one significant limitation that prevents me from keeping it. The unit does not support QHD 2560×1440 resolution. I tried multiple configuration options, but nothing worked. My Dell U2515H monitor clearly reports that it cannot operate at this resolution through this KVM. As a result, both my Mac Mini and my Windows PC were forced to run at Full HD — and while the image quality was fine, this resolution is unacceptable for my workflow.

On the positive side, the Mac Mini worked flawlessly when connected via Thunderbolt/USB-C, and all other supported resolutions (Full HD and 4K) functioned perfectly.

Support was polite but unable to confirm whether 2560×1440 should work, and the product description does not explicitly mention this limitation.

Overall, this is a high-quality device with excellent performance — just not suitable for users who need QHD.

title: 3.0 out of 5 stars
text:
Purchased as a used-like new DVD-RW device from Amazon, the drive arrived bent and not able to eject the disc tray. An hour's careful bending of the very flimsy sheet metal typical of these 9.5 mm thick drives, adjustment of the ejection latch, and repeated installation - removal from a desktop tower, yielded a unit both physically and electrically "up to snuff". The drive plays back and records as expected.

This drive arrived with the front bezel left retaining tang (plastic) broken off, and the right tang bent through failure. The front bezel flopped free during first installation of the drive. The bezel is now super-glued in place, AFTER the required sheet metal and ejection latch repair.

This CD / DVD-RW unit is identified by Windows 10 Device Manager (from the drive firmware) as HL-DT-ST DVD-RW GU70N, a Hitachi-LG Data Storage device. The name "OSGEAR appears nowhere except on the wholly inadequate zip-lock bag in which the drive was packed, and in Amazon's advertising.

All-in-all, a perfectly usable DVD-RW drive for a pittance in cost, but requiring judicious repair by the buyer to be made usable.

I was going to send this back as installation was not easy. I decided to try again and have my wife help me who has worked with wall paper many times. I tried following the enclosed quick instructions but that didn't work. So here's what I did and maybe this helps:
1) Make sure the screen is clean...... make it pristine clean and take your time.
2) Lay the monitor FLAT .... it is easier to work that way since the films stickiness will drive you crazy if the monitor is upright.
3) Remove one side of the plastic of the film exposing the stick side. Start from the SIDE since you are working with less material at one time and it is thus easier to work with. Check the alignment at the very start or the film will run crooked and you'll be upset.
4) It's a good idea to have help with an extra pair of hands otherwise this will drive you crazy as you try to smooth out the bubbles as you slowly adhere a small piece of the film at a time.
5) In the end, I don't think you'll remove all the bubbles but they won't be obvious once the screen is ON.
6) The concept is fine but in the end, the small bubble were impossible to remove perfectly.
7) My goal was to remedy the reflection in my monitors. It worked.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
This is somewhat expensive for what amounts to a plastic sheet that goes over your screen, but if the price matches your needs, this is a good value that will protect your screen from passers-by quite well.

This privacy screen filter comes with two installation methods - one utilizing tabs that stick on the sides (outside the screen edge) which let you slide the filter on and off, and another that simply attaches it to your screen with some very small strips of double sided adhesive. Once you've puzzled through the instructions and picked which way you want to install it, it only takes a minute or two to get it onto your screen. The size matches my screen's specs, as expected - as long as you pick the right size for your screen, it will fit perfectly. It does a good job of protecting your screen from anyone trying to view it from the side, darkening quickly to make anything over a 30º angle to either side illegible. Despite this security feature, it has almost no effect on your screen's brightness - it's not zero effect, but it's akin to darkening your screen by about 3% to 5%. It's very well made, with no blemishes, and it includes a protective plastic layer on both sides of the screen cover that you need to peel off when instructed. Overall I'd say this a great choice if you value your privacy and regularly go out in public!

The only downside I've found with this screen filter is the fact that the instructions regarding installation are a bit confusing. Installation itself is easy, but this definitely could have done with some labeling and separation of parts - even some small plastic bags labeling the different installation methods would have helped a lot, but the instructions themselves could also have been more clear, because as it is they're spread out and arranged a bit confusingly. It's a minor issue, but critical, because if you can't figure out how to install it right then you're not going to be able to use it at all. I don't have a touchscreen to test this with, just a regular laptop screen.

There are no magnets in this. It attaches either with adhesive 'tabs' that go off your screen and on the side of your monitor, or via some double sided strips that go directly onto your screen.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
purchased two of these to replace self-built gaming machines following a house fire. I've been building gaming machines for 25 years. Never bought a pre-made system myself. I consider this an act of humility :). Only because I don't have the tools or workspace to do it myself, not being able to live at home at the moment.

Pros:
1. I love the top vent cover. It goes across almost the entire top, and is magnetically attached. very flexible and easy to remove for cleaning.

2. Performance for the dollar is spectacular.
all settings at maximum:
-- I can play pubg on my 2K display at the monitor's max of 180FPS, consistently.
-- Elder Scrolls Oblivion Remastered, even with HDR and ray tracing, 60-70 FPS consistently.
3. Lighting is beautiful. The included MSI app is very easy to operate to choose different light patterns and colors.

The only issues I have, I found consistently across brands:
1. I couldn't find a gaming system with 5.25 bays. I previously had BDXL drives, and none of the newer pre-built systems have 5.25 bays, so I'll be using my external USB drive
2. Adding storage. The wire management at first glance is fantastic. only when you remove the non-window side panel do you see where they crammed all the extra wires for other devices, along with some tiny space for hard drives or SSD's. I have big man-hands and had a little trouble pulling out the cables I want, and then trying to fit them back in once I'd connected one of my salvaged SATA ssd's. I think moving forward, I will buy a PCI-E M.2 card, and add an M.2 drive instead, if not just for speed, but so I don't have to deal with the cabling.
3. Bloatware. I was surprised to find Norton still rearing its ugly head. it was the first to go, followed by the Office 365 trial. The latter could not be easily removed from the add/remove programs. it listed every available language as one to be removed. I ended up downloading a tool I use from work: Office Scrubber. A utility from Microsoft that runs a separate script to remove all things office.
4. non-back panel ports. I'm not a fan of ports on top of the case. Practically ensures they'll get caked with dust if something isn't always plugged in. Considering getting dummy USB port inserts.
5. Still has some USB 2.0 ports. WHY on earth!? I have two 8TB drives I use to back up movies, family photos and videos, and once one is updated, I use Free File Sync to update the other drive. I found myself with a countdown timer of days, only for me to realize one of them was connected to a 2.0 port. Switched to the USB 3.2 ports, and it was down to less than 30 minutes. (also has a PS/2 port...again WHY?)

Final note: Not the fault of the system, but still noting it since the componentry is part of the issue. For best refresh rate on your screen, use DisplayPort. the HDMI version on this board is slower than DisplayPort.

Overall, VERY satisfied. again Bought two of these, one for me and the wife.

title: 2.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I purchased this specifically to run pfSense, and initially I was extremely impressed. The OS booted up flawlessly, and performance was absolutely excellent - a huge step up from my previous Intel N100 based system. I was thrilled with the low power consumption and fantastic temperatures. It truly blew my N100 system out of the water in terms of speed, heat, and efficiency.

However, and this is a big however, the built-in Intel 226 NIC is a serious weak point. I experienced significant packet loss during even basic Internet upload speed tests. Worse, the NIC would occasionally completely fail for around 5 minutes, taking the entire network down with it. After researching the issue, it appears to be related to Active State Power Management (ASPM). Unfortunately, there's no option to disable ASPM in the BIOS, and attempting to disable it within pfSense itself simply shuts the NIC off entirely.

Adding to the issues, the fan noise is quite loud by default. Despite updating to the latest BIOS, the aggressive fan curve remained problematic. Thankfully, the BIOS does allow for custom fan curve adjustments, and dialing it back completely solved the noise issue. Given the incredibly low temperatures this device maintains, a less aggressive default curve is desperately needed from MSI.

While the core performance and efficiency are outstanding, the unreliable NIC (due to the unaddressable ASPM issue) is a deal-breaker. This device could be perfect for a pfSense build, but this flaw unfortunately holds it back.

This review is for MSI Cubi NUC AI+ Barebones Mini PC: Intel Core Ultra 7-258V, 32GB Memory, WiFi 6E, BT 5.3, Thunderbolt 4, Type-C, Copilot Button: Black (2MG-003BUS).

Purchased this as a replacement for my 4 year old Dell OptiPlex with Core i5-11500 CPU in a hope to get similar performance in a smaller form-factor. Well, the Intel Core Ultra 7-258V delivers the performance but the Cubi's cooling system is not so great: the fan noise is constant and annoying if you keep the PC at one hand length that is required to use the built-in fingerprint reader.

The fan rarely changes the speed but even when the system is idle it is producing high-pitch noise that is very irritating in quiet home/office environment. It is not coming from a defective fan but rather from the physics of the fan (I have similar issue with my X1 Carbon Aura that sports the same CPU when the fan is kicking on high speed).

Otherwise, this is a nice and compact system that is well equipped to handle some local AI tasks (once these become available in software, these is almost nothing that uses NPU at the moment).

The system does not come with Copilot button despite the title (should be purchased separately), and it looks like the m.2 slot is Gen. 5 x4 (haven't tested it with Gen. 5 SSD, Samsung EVO Plus gave me about 7000Mbs R/W.

I had to return the Cubi because of fan noise.

text:
Overall this is a great laptop. It runs everything I throw at it smoothly and without issues. As usual, MSI has top-quality products and this laptop is no exception. They beat out an asus laptop I wanted on a few points:

- Better keyboard programmability than competitors
- The trackpad feels smooth and amazing
- Lighting options are better than competitors
- 4k screen with excellent quality
- Windows hello camera
- It just feels and looks great

There are only a few things that cause me to give 4 stars instead of 5:

- Steelseries software is very buggy, and you cannot save your keyboard presets. Since it's buggy it may need to be reinstalled. If so you will lose all presets, and there is no way to save or export these settings at all. This is a major failure and worth losing a star on its own. This should be easy to solve but seems to be a basic failure of the software design.
- PD charging does not work as advertised. It worked at first, then stopped working 2 days after I got the laptop. MSI recommended I return it to the retailer. The new laptop also fails to charge over USB-c or thunderbolt.
- The keyboard brightness is too low. When you press the FN key, the top row of function keys lights up solid red and very bright. Unfortunately this is the only time the keys get this bright. Even on the brightest setting, the keyboard seems to be intentionally dimmer than the possible maximum. This causes the keyboard to be dimmer than competitors like asus, and unfortunately MSI seems to use altered images when showing the keyboard in advertisements to make it look brighter.
- The fan is extremely loud when it gets going.
- Lighting does not integrate well with other services
- Steelseries audio is poorly designed and not very useful.
- No ability to wake from sleep when the laptop is closed. I use a dock and close the laptop. I should be able to move the mouse or type on the keyboard and wake up the computer, but this basic option is not available in the bios.

Overall I think this is the best laptop in its class and price range over its competitors.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
Form Factor & Build Quality
Both machines share a similar footprint, but there are some notable ergonomic differences:

Trackpad: MSI's is centered, while Lenovo's is offset left. Preference may vary.

MSI Fans: Slightly whinier under load, but the system runs cooler overall.

Pen: MSI includes the pen in the box... Lenovo charges extra.

Build: MSI’s fit and finish is solid, with clever hinge design that slightly elevates the laptop for better airflow.

Screen: MSI wins here. It's brighter, slightly warmer tone, and excellent clarity. Some reviews knock the large bottom bezel, but it’s clearly intentional and part of the hinge-lift design.

Speakers
Lenovo wins easily. MSI’s speakers are thin and underwhelming. They'll do in a pinch, but Lenovo's are significantly fuller and louder.

Software & Updates
Lenovo Vantage is miles ahead. It handles driver, firmware, and BIOS updates with minimal user intervention.

MSI relies on manual driver downloads from its website. BIOS updates require old-school flashing via USB, which is functional but not consumer-friendly.

Initial Setup Experience
Lenovo’s setup is smoother and less time consuming.

MSI required a lot more manual effort, verifying and installing updates. This meant a day or two of off and on tinkering versus a few hours on Lenovo.

Performance
MSI AI 365:
Cinebench R23 Multi-core: ~18,090
Single-core: ~1,983–2,000
Single-core runs at ~24W and spikes cores over 5GHz, so it's likely maxed out.

Lenovo 12700H:

Multi-core: ~9,700
Single-core: ~1,737
Performance has degraded over time, and is below online averages (typically 13,000–15,000), likely due to sustained throttling and limited power delivery.

Thermals, Power & Fan Behavior
MSI:
Holds steady temps in the 65–72°C range during loads.
Idle wattage is impressively low (~5W).
Power draw under full load can hit 50W with no thermal runaway.
The fan is quieter overall, in that it doesn't spin up as often, and while it has a "wheesh" tone when it does, you won’t hear it over a basic laptop cooler stand.

Lenovo:
Idles efficiently (also ~5–6W), but under load it quickly spikes to 100°C, triggers throttling, and can’t maintain sustained performance.
Fan has a more "whoosh" character and stays active more often. I like the sound of the Lenovo fan better.

Cooling Solution
Lenovo likely has the better-engineered cooling system, but it’s simply not enough for the 12700H + Arc combo.

MSI runs warm on the left side of the keyboard (where the CPU sits), but it’s nowhere near "hot" — and performs much better overall.

Final Verdict
If you're comfortable managing your own updates via the MSI support site, the MSI Summit AI 365 is a fantastic machine. It’s easily twice as fast as what it replaces, with excellent build quality, efficient thermals, and standout performance from the Ryzen AI 9 365.

It's not perfect... the fans are less impressive, and the software update experience lags far behind Lenovo's Vantage platform, but the hardware/price makes up for it.

Bottom Line:
The Summit AI 365 is one of the best price to performance laptops currently available with the new Ryzen AI chips. Even ASUS’s Zenbook with the AI 9 370 can't match its performance due to inferior thermals. MSI nailed the balance here... if they improve their software experience, they'll be a top contender for SMB and prosumer users alike.

PS: The new Ryzen CPU's can have very different performance characteristics depending on manufacturer tuning. Asus, as mentioned earlier, tends to lean into the thin + light + battery style. MSI on the other hand went for a more balanced approach, with more robust form factor and increased performance.

4 Month Update:
Pros: No problems and fwiw this was an open box unit. Very Very fast. Runs cooler than my old Intel by a lot. Battery is also WAY WAY better.
Cons: Fan is still a little whiny, though it hasn't become worse. The MSI Center still lags behind the bigger brands for ease-of-update. They also can't get the aspect ratio of the MSI Center correct. Bios updates still require flashing via a USB, and since it's a new chip you WANT those updates.
Overall: Still satisfied the AI 9 365 is a great chip and the Summit is a good platform for it. Will update if I have issues.

text:
Bios options are lacking. I was expecting something better, especially from a reputable hardware manufacturer such as MSI. As one of the three major global system board producers, their bios options within firmware are typically much more robust, and not so limited such as this. At first I was thinking maybe the limited options are related to the N200 platform or chipset, but I've definitely seen other devices with the same CPU from different manufacturers offer more robust configuration.

But aside from the limited configuration, the performance is also just not there for me. The device is hard-locked to a lower wattage as it's passively cooled. This has a major effect in 3D gaming. You shouldn't expect much 3D gaming with this, but older games are typically viable on this CPU with higher wattage or TDP. But not so with this.
4k YouTube videos play just fine and the system does indeed perform well otherwise. But the hurdles you have to go through just to unlock a slightly higher TDP are quite disappointing. The system doesn't need much more power to perform better. You don't need to run this at 30w just to game. But you do need a sustainable PL2 power curve which keeps GPU clocks boosted and TDP only 1 or 2 watts above the default TDP of 6w.

Here is a screenshot of using shady and highly dangerous Chinese firmware hacking tools you will need just to run 32bit old-school classic Skyrim :)

You could also try a safer application known as "universal x86 tuning utility" or maybe perhaps you could also use something known as "throttlestop" though be aware as these may be able to bypass certain limitations you still might be hard-locked out of a few other limitations and of course you also have to deal with the thermals generated from this devices suboptimal cooling :)

text:
I would highly recommend this laptop! You get what you pay for, assuming you get the right thing. I've seen that some people received faulty units or a used one after buying it new, and those are real problems--they're not problems with what this product is, though; they're separate issues. I expect that, once more people buy this thing, the quality control and shipping issues will be smoothed out. Maybe give it time and buy this later, but definitely buy this!

Several of the bad reviews this laptop has gotten have been about the laptop's design, like its weight or noise level. This is a gaming laptop; this device's nature is like that of a gaming laptop. Both attributes are within a normal range for what gaming laptops are meant to be; you're buying portable desktop power. I've played games on this thing with max video settings and I don't think the fans were at even half their maximum speed, and the games ran flawlessly, well above the screen's refresh rate. Noise should not be an issue, unless you'd set the fans to max and complain. Everything I've thrown at this rig hasn't even come close to turning the fans to max, so I'm not sure what you'd do that would need it🤷

I haven't tested the battery life, but...come on. This is a gaming laptop; you're not buying it for battery life. Take the charger with you, and a full desktop-level battlestation is yours to take anywhere. I'm a student and want to do my work(game development and 3d asset pipelines) in multiple places, and this rig will let me do it with ease. Students- you should tell your parents a "decent everyday laptop for casual office use" costs $3k!

The screen is easily the best screen I've had! 1440p with a few extra pixels on the bottom to make it a 16:10 aspect ratio give me a huge amount of screen space, and I feel much more comfortable doing art, games and dev work on this rig than on my previous 15" gaming laptop. The color accuracy is also amazing; everything looks more vibrant!

We had an old laptop that died recently and wouldn't be worth repairing, so while the October Prime Days event was on I looked for something that should be somewhat 'future proof' with good specs at a price less than $1000. I picked the MSI Katana A15 AI 15.6” 144Hz FHD Gaming Laptop with the Ryzen 7-9945HS and NVIDIA Geforce RTX 4060, 32Gb RAM, and 1TB SSD.
It was on sale for $879 plus tax at the time, which was a really good price for the specs.

The screen is a bit more 'letter box' shape than I'd really like, but that's the only thing I can find to whine about. It's a bit heavy compared to some, but that isn't an issue for us.
It runs all our small business office and accounting software silently, without the cooling system kicking in at all. The only time it cools itself is when playing graphic intensive games, and IMHO the fan noise isn't bad at all. Most of the time it sits on a multi fan cooling pad, but even without that turned on the laptop never gets particularly hot.
All in all, it was a great deal, so if it's on sale for less than $900 again, snap it up. Even at around $1050 I think it's still a worthy contender.

Ive used MSI for years motherboard, monitors and video cards. This laptop felt like a safe choice to let my kids use it since we trust the brand. Specs are specs and I wanted a brand that I’ve used.
What makes the Cyborg A15 a great MSI machine is what's underneath. We know that MSI is focused on efficient cooling and stable power and even in this more budget-friendly chassis, that core quality shows:
1. Reliable Guts: The combination of the modern AMD Ryzen 7 260 and the RTX 5050 is good enough for my kids usage. It handles data quickly thanks to the 1TB NVMe SSD and the 16GB DDR5 RAM, meaning my kids aren't waiting on load screens—they're just playing. This stability and speed are exactly what we expect from MSI's engineering.
2. The Cooling Mindset: Like any good gaming laptop or desktop, the cooling is designed for performance. Even though the fans can get loud under load (well not that load), that's just MSI's Cooler Boost technology doing its job: the thermals are good enough for the GPU and CPU so they don’t throttle during gaming sessions. That stability is what you need.
This isn't just reliable; it's also wrapped in a package that immediately appealed to the kids, which is the perfect mix for a gift:
• The whole translucent black look is a fantastic piece of cyberpunk flair. The kids immediately gravitated to it. It makes the laptop feel unique and exciting—far from the generic black boxes
• Gaming Experience: The 144Hz screen delivers a smooth playing experience for modern gaming, making even casual play feel responsive and high-end.
The Trade-Off for all Gaming Laptops
If you've used gaming laptops before, you know the biggest trade-off is usually the battery life. This is no exception. It’s an effective gaming laptop placement, but for peak performance, it needs to be plugged in. This is less about quality and more about physics: if you want high power in a slim body, you need a constant power source. If you just use the laptop normally you could get around 4 hours for battery life.

text: Since I've been using this laptop it's performance has been more than sufficient. I've been using it for day to day tasks as well as gaming. For gaming I've been playing games like Ori and the Will of the Wisps, Team Sonic Racing, etc. and they all run fine at 1080p on high settings. Granted these aren't AAA titles that demand a ton but they do run fine at high settings. I did notice that the laptop like to default to the built in AMD GPU instead of the Nvidia 5050 and I had to manually set the laptop to use the 5050 over the AMD. One thing I did notice is that it seems like the 5050 seems to run games at a slightly lower fps than the AMD. This leads into power. It is significantly powerful enough to do daily tasks plus some gaming. I have noticed though that the 16 GB of RAM seems to get eaten up pretty quickly though. It could definitely use 32 GB or Windows 11 needs to be debloated. Temperatures seem to be pretty stable as well. I haven't any over heating issues and the fans don't spin up much except for when gaming. Temps seem stable holding around 37-39 Celsius when doing normal tasks. It also has plenty of venting on the bottom of the case to help keep those temps down. I'm also able to watch 1440p videos with no issues or dropped frames when watching on YouTube. The screen clarity is also really nice and with the 144hz refresh rate it's very easy on the eyes and movement is very smooth. I haven't noticed any tearing issues with videos or games. Looks wise the case is nice. It's got several semi transparent stop on the case to see some of the internals. It is also pretty well built as well. Also so you can access the extra slots to upgrade your RAM (yes it is upgradable) or swap out your NVME drive. Size and weight wise it is comfortable as well. Not too heavy and not overly thick. Finally the webcam, even though being a 720p camera, does produce a very good image quality. You can tell they spent a little bit of money on the sensor quality. You do have to have pretty good ambient light though to get a good picture quality when I tested this. Another issue is that the location of the mouse track pad is in a odd place and is pretty large. When typing on the keyboard part of my hand actually resets on the track pad. Because of this I've had the cursor move and had accidental clicks. Poorly designed. Awful assembly documentation. Front panel connection cable is a joke.
Memory channel B defective

About me: I am a Systems Engineer with more than 25 years of experience making my own PCs.

A few moths ago I built an 9950X on a Asus Strix X870E no issues at all with that system. Rock solid.

This time I decided to make a second workstation with an 9950X3D and this MSI Board

Te board came poorly packaged on Amazon box without any cushioning. The Board box itself came without any seal altough after inspecting it everything seemed fine.

I assembled the PC as I allways do (I do this job about 3-4 times per year as I keep upgrading my systems for better work performance).

The board has no clear identifiers on their internal connections for USB, Audio and front panel. The Dimm slots are not identified either (the Asus Board is as clear as it can be) so I downloaded the manual on my phone to check the connections (the box didn't include any basic reference printed documentation but MSI choose to put some cartoon stickers jajaj). The connections in general are mostly cryptic acronyms so If you are unexperienced don't get this board by any means.

I finished the build and tried to boot the system to configure the BIOS. It keept giving C5 error code on the diagnostic panel. After a lot of trial and error I found out that the memory channel B was not working. Removing the memory from that slot booted wihout issues (I have 4 memory kits available so I was able to make many tests). I suspected bent pins on the socket (I was very, very carful installing the CPU as I know how easy is to damage the socket), so. I removed the cooler and the CPU and using a magnifying glass inspected the socket. didn't found any issues with it as I was fearing even if I was extremely careful on the CPU install.

Second step I removed the board from the PC case and inspected it. No physical issues where found. The memory slots don't cross the back of the board so no shorts are possible either.

So, the board is just a lemon that wasn't properly tested on factoy and I lost a complete day of work.

I would also mention the stiffness of power connectors and the memory slots itselfs. It was very hard to disconnect the components. Specially the power connector. Comparing this roughness to the Strix is night and day.

So, I am now dealing with returning this POS to Amazon and getting a refund.

If you want a secure experience get the Asus. I am done with MSI and would not buy again any boards from this brand.

title: 3.0 out of 5 stars
text:
You really get what you pay for with this, but at the same time it’s really good for the price it is.

I’ll start off with the bad: this thing was cheap ($100 on Prime Day), and if you know computers you know 200hz monitors at this price range can be sketchy, but MSI is a known and trusted brand. However, it’s so cheaply made. It’s all plastic and it honestly feels like it could break at any moment just by looking at it in a funny way. The OSD button in the back is a joke, it’s extremely wobbly, like it can fall off at any moment. It’s also a pain to maneuver around with it since it’s not sturdy, so you can end up moving or pressing when you didn’t mean to.

And oh my goodness that stand is godawful. It doesn’t go up or down or move left or right. Thankfully I bought a VESA stand to mitigate this, and now it’s a lot more comfortable to game with.

There’s not much to say about the OSD itself. There are your normal preset gaming modes and crosshairs, but I don’t really mess with that stuff, I’d much prefer to mess with the settings myself. It has an AI mode which I honestly have no clue what it really does, nor do I honestly care; I don’t like to put filters or post processing stuff like that on my monitors.

But oh man this thing actually looks good. The colors are bright and saturated, the contrast is very good, and 200 hz actually makes a huge difference. I’ve played with 144 and 165 hz monitors and I don’t think I could go back. I can actually feel the difference in refresh rate and my games run silky smooth. I normally play fighting games and shooters, and if you know about those games, you know that fast refresh rates actually matter. If you’re in the 120-144 hz range and you play these types of games, I highly recommend making the switch to this.

I also calibrated the colors and brightness and it looks much better than out the box.

Overall, don’t expect a tough or modern looking monitor; it’s $100 for a reason. But I truthfully think that this might be a budget banger.

It was SO HOT I burned myself touching it. I tried a final attempt at playing unplugged and then plugging it in to charge as needed before the power cord overheated and it could not even charge fast enough to stop the battery drain even without a lowest graphics, low brightness, and energy efficient modes. Everything else is great, but the battery is a gigantic downside.

title: 3.0 out of 5 stars
text:
NOTE: This is a 24-hour review. I will update it within the next 6 months to reflect whether my experience remains positive, neutral, or becomes negative. I am not sponsored, nor was this item given to me for free; I paid for it with my own money.

The monitor is gorgeous straight out of the box. It's spacious and a big upgrade for anyone coming from a 21- or 22-inch screen. I can confidently say that this particular monitor will be an improvement in terms of size and visual impact. However, I’m giving it a 3 out of 5 instead of a perfect score, and here’s why:

While the monitor offers a lot of features, the placement of the ports is awkward. Instead of being directly accessible on the back like a traditional monitor, the ports are hidden, which makes connecting cables unnecessarily frustrating. I assume this design is meant for users who want to push the monitor close to the wall without damaging the cables, but it comes at the cost of convenience.

After turning the monitor on and fiddling with settings, switching between the GPU control panel and the monitor’s menu, I have to say I’m a bit disappointed. Here's why:

Even though the picture quality is sharp, the monitor has a noticeable yellow tint. If you're someone who prefers using your computer in a dark room, this yellowish cast is especially obvious. I spent a long time adjusting the settings, trying to eliminate it, but doing so made the display overly bright and uncomfortable to look at. Reducing the brightness helped, but then the colors became distorted. I read through forums, watched videos and shorts, and dug through reviews looking for a solution, but so far, no luck. Maybe I misunderstood what this monitor was offering, but it honestly feels more like a VA panel than an IPS one.

Ironically, my old HP Pavilion 22xi 21.5-inch IPS monitor was much easier on the eyes. The colors were beautiful, even if slightly washed out, and I never had to deal with this kind of eye strain.

If I had the option to return this monitor, I probably would, but I’ll keep it to avoid the hassle. Most buyers feel the same way when it comes to expensive electronics: once you buy them online, you’re stuck. If there were an option for a partial refund, I’d gladly take it. That way, both sides would come out ahead. But as it stands, I’m stuck with it.

Don’t get me wrong, it’s a beautiful monitor with vibrant colors. But the yellow tint and excessive brightness have significantly hurt my overall satisfaction. When I bought it, there were no reviews available, so I took a gamble. Lesson learned: Never buy a product without hundreds of reviews.

That said, my negative experience comes from someone who primarily uses a computer in the dark. If you tend to play or work with the lights on, your experience may be entirely different.

title: 1.0 out of 5 stars
text:
Gonna crash out for a minute, here's my story with the MSI Herald-BE card. For reference, I spent the better part of a decade in IT/systems before changing professions (couldn't handle any more network printer error tickets), so hopefully my troubleshooting can help save someone else a headache. If not, TL;DR is at the bottom.

I spent the better part of tonight trying to get this card to work in my wife's gaming PC. Brand-spankin'-new, fast modern technology. Fire up the PC, Wi-fi picks right up, but no BT. Probably a driver right? Pick up the driver from MSI, run the setup and get a "no suitable drivers" error. Ok, weird. Double check the connection for the provided cable between the card and the board, it's in there. Check device manager, nothing showing with errors. Use the included driver CD (gross, literally had to find my external CD drive) and ran the setup, only detects the Wi-fi portion. Check the support page on MSI (again) and sure enough the BT should be showing up separately from the Wi-fi for drivers. Restart and check BIOS to make sure nothing dumb happened; USB port is active. Restart and go to ASUS for motherboard drivers (ASUS Prime X570-P is the part). Search for chipset drivers and restart, still nothing.

I start looking on forums for issues with this card. Most of the "BT not working" trouble was from people not realizing you have to plug the USB cable to your mobo, then it works no problem. Not working for me, so I dive deeper. Cross reference the mobo with this card and there's TWO posts about it (which is 2 more than I expected). One post refers to the other as a solution, so I cross my fingers and read the thread.

A few people with the same mobo are trying to figure out what's going on with the USB connections. One user starts testing between the two USB connection ports on the board and finds that one of them works flawlessly, the other not at all. Changes to another device, same outcome, so it sounds like the port. I check the port number (USB11 if you're wondering), that's the port I'm having an issue with too! Sweet hallelujah, we're getting somewhere! Not the somewhere I wanna be, but still it's progress. Since I am using the other mobo port for the USB ports on the PC case itself, I'm stuck figuring out what's up with this second port in particular.

Further on someone posts a link to the mobo manual, calls out the page for the USB port connections on the board, and tells everyone to look it over. I get to the page and confirm that's what I'm looking at on my own board, but a bunch of "NC"'s catch my eye on the pin description section. I go back to the forum, and the user explains the NC ports mean there's no connection. NO. CONNECTION. THEY LITERALLY DIDN'T WIRE THE BOTTOM PINS ON THIS BOARD.

/sigh

So I look back at the cable just like the forum users and sure enough, the one provided with the Wi-Fi card uses the lower "NC" pins. Well, at least I know why nothing is detecting. I keep reading on the forum and a few users noted that it's simple enough to just move the wires on the provided cable from the bottom to the top pins, so I give that a shot. It was easier than I expected, and my hopes rise.

I plug everything back in; adjusted pin connection to the mobo and original connection to the Wi-Fi card. Fire the PC up and WE HAVE AN UNKNOWN DEVICE! Surely this has solved it. I pat myself on the back, down my Red Bull, and click the BT driver setup once again. I breathe a sigh of relief as the software loads and I click the "Install" button....and nothing happens. The button is greyed out...."No suitable drivers"...

This....can't be happening....I take another breath, but this time I'm nervous. I go back to device manager and tell it to update manually, selecting my driver folder. No change. I run the driver CD software, does not detect the BT. I go BACK to the mobo manual and look over the pin values, then double check that I moved the right color wires into the right pins. I spent a few minutes learning about USB cable colors and their corresponding functions (power vs data) to make sure. I got it right, everything aligns. I shut the PC down and pull the cable out again. Maybe I needed to move the wires on both ends of the cable? Worth a shot right?

I move the wires just like before and everything lines up just as it did, now just on the top row of pins for both ends of the cable. I triple check and make sure the wires are pushed all the way in, everything feels good. I plug the cable back in and fire up the rig, going straight into device manager. The unknown device is gone!

HALLELUJAH! It's gone! It's gone.....it's gone? Where is it? No "Bluetooth" device is listed, nothing new showing up under network adapters...what?

I check the cables one last time, they're firmly seated. I swap the ends between the card and the board, scan for changes, nothing. Wi-fi worked the entire time. I am 100% at a loss here, and I know this is absolutely due to the fact that the pins are not connected on that mobo port.

TL;DR the MSI Herald-BE Wi-Fi/Bluetooth card isn't compatible with the ASUS PRIME X570-P motherboard because ASUS is cheap and/or stupid.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
Cards like this are mostly just a simple adapter for connecting the underlying WiFi+Bluetooth chip to your computer - PCI Express x1 for the WiFi, and a little USB pin cable for the Bluetooth. As such, there's only 4 ways that they're meaningfully different:

1. The chip. There are two WiFi 7 chips generally considered the best on the market today. The standard advice is "get the Qualcomm if you have an AMD processor, or the Intel if you have an Intel processor." This is the Qualcomm one. My system is AMD on Windows 11, and I've had no issues with it at all.
2. The included antenna. It's not exactly small, but not huge either. The magnetic base is convenient, but also pretty standard for these. It does what it needs to.
3. The drivers. Others have mentioned here that downloading the drivers off MSI's site is a better option than the included disc - which is unfortunate because "downloading" is why you buy one of these things in the first place. I can't really take points off for this, as I didn't even try the drivers on the disc, but keep it in mind if you don't have access to another computer and a thumb drive.
4. The price. It may not be true when you read this, but as of 2026-01-30 this is the cheapest I've seen for a WiFi 7 card.

If you have an AMD system and a way to get ahold of the drivers, just get this one. It won't disappoint.

I used the MSI PRO B550M-VC WiFi ProSeries motherboard in my most recent home server build, and it has turned out to be a great fit for what I needed. As a dad running a small home lab out of the corner of my office (with four kids and a dog occasionally bumping into my gear), I needed a motherboard that could balance reliability, expandability, and a small footprint, and this one delivered.

One of the biggest selling points for me was the multiple PCIe x16 slots. I’m using one for a GPU (for some light Plex transcoding and occasional AI tinkering) and another for an HBA card to expand my drive capacity. Another huge win: the SATA ports. I’ve currently got six drives hooked up, four for bulk media storage, one for VMs, and one for parity, and the board handled it all without any splitter drama. There’s room to grow, which is a relief because these kids keep filling the Plex server with every animated series ever created.

The onboard WiFi was a nice bonus. I’m wired in most of the time, but having WiFi as a fallback during router reboots or for quick setup made things easier.

Build quality feels solid, and the BIOS was straightforward to navigate. I had zero issues getting my Ryzen 7 5700G up and running, and I haven’t had to touch the setup since, just how I like it for a home server I want to forget is running in the background.

If you’re looking for a dependable, feature-packed micro-ATX board for a home server or general-purpose system with multiple PCIe devices and lots of storage, this is a fantastic option. It’s done everything I’ve asked of it, and more, without fuss.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
Great value for $110-ish! It supports 3 onboard connections to 3 monitors (HDMI, DisplayPort, and VGA), with an APU such as Ryzen 7 5700G. HDMI is 2.1, but DisplayPort is only 1.2, so check on your monitor's resolution. The motherboard comes with BIOS version 7C95vH8, so the BIOS does not need to be updated to support Ryzen 7 5700G. Version 7C95vH0 and above supports this CPU/APU.

It supports up to 8 SATA storage devices, so it's great for future expansion on HDD or SSD. It works perfectly with a case like Phanteks Eclipse G500A (This case also provides front panel type-C USB connector to this board). Note that the M.2_1 slot support Gen3 PCIe SSD, unless your CPU/APU supports Gen4. Practically there is not much difference between Gen3 and Gen4 PCIe SSD anyways for either gaming or daily use. The compatibility list on the MSI website was last updated on FEB 2023, and the tech support is not very helpful on finding anything other than that list. The newer versions of DRAM should mostly be compatible, and you just have to plug them in and see if they pass the onboard EZ LED light debug checking sequence at booting. If so, then your DRAM is good to go.

Caution: Do NOT install the B550 chipset drivers through the MSI Centre prompt! If you do it, it will mess up your system and make it not bootable. Then you'd have to restore the system to the last recovery point. Just go with the drivers on the MSI website (and the AMD website for your CPU/APU), and you are good to go.

text:
I have a love/hate relationship with this mobo. Once it’s set up, it works like a dream!

It comes with a very basic BIOS which doesn’t allow it to operate much at all. To get it up and running, you need to install the latest version of BIOS from a flash-drive. That means that you have to have access to a working computer that you can use to download the latest BIOS onto a flash-drive before you can upload it onto the mobo. It was a complicated process for this novice, but now that I’ve done it, not so very difficult after all!

The next problem was that the mobo won’t access my old HDD’s because it operates UEFI protocol. According to the manual, which I had to download onto my phone (!), the protocol can be switched to accept other versions, but my initial attempts have been unsuccessful. I therefore had to download Windows onto a flash-drive, via another computer, and upload it onto the mobo.

Because the mobo is cutting-edge, it has 2 iSSD ports. I had bought a 1TB iSSD as part of the build and the installation was fairly straightforward, but fiddley.

And now the ‘love’ bit!!! The build powers up in 15 seconds and powers down in 5 seconds. The in-built WiFi works well, even though one of the antennae is loose - I’d have to take the mobo out of the case to tighten the nut!

Although I’ve not given it a stern test, it performs all the ordinary tasks effortlessly and shows every sign that it could allow my R5 CPU to fly!!!

One last thing; the BIOS for this board isn’t on the MSI UK list - you have to get it from the MSI US list!!! As I said at the start - a love/hate relationship!!!

text:
有線GM41のレビューです。セールで1980円という値段に惹かれつい買ってしまいました。
高耐久マイクロスイッチ、高DPIセンサー、軽量編みケーブル、6ボタン、色調整可なLED発光
ここまで対応して2000円しないメーカーマウス初めて見たので。
実際に使ってみても不満な点はありませんでした。
機能もパーツも使用感も全体的に良いのに安すぎて逆に誤解されるような幸薄感すら覚えます。
非セール価格でも安いので有線マウス買い替えを考えている方にはおすすめします。

以下使用感の詳細です。
ーーーーーーーーーーーーーーーーーーーーーーーーーーーーーーーー
ケーブルも本体も偏りなく軽いのでワイヤレスから切り替えましたが有線の引っ張り感は薄いです。
クリックの押下もブレを感じず軽く反応し、安価なタクトスイッチとはまた違った押下感が気持ちいいです。音は普通にカチカチなります。
サイドも材質が異なるので特に滑りはなく、傾斜は親指が抜けやすい事も引っ掛かり過ぎる事もないように感じました。
サイド2ボタンはクリックボタンに比べてブレやすく押下も少し深くて若干安っぽい感じはあります。
マウス全体のサイズは縦に長めなので、手の小さい方には少し微妙かもしれません。
指先から手首まで20cm弱と大きめの私の手でちょうどすっぽり収まる感じです。
ホイールは一般的な段階式でスクロールとクリック音も小さい方だとは思いますが静音ほどではないです。
LEDはデフォだと派手ですが独自ソフト入れずにマウス単体で発光調整可能です。個人的にこの点はありがたかったです。

最高のマウス！とは言いませんが、有線としても使用感がかなり軽く
耐久度の高いマイクロスイッチと編みケーブル持ちの6ボタンマウスがこの価格帯なのは本当に安いです。

title: 4.0 out of 5 stars
text:
This board is almost perfect, at least for me. My system has dual GPUs with one primary and one supporting in the second (physical) x16 slot. For what I do, the reduced bandwidth is acceptable, considering this is a consumer platform. However, I did not read the manual for this board before purchasing. Turns out, the second NVMe slot disables the second x16 slot when used. That was rather annoying to troubleshoot. My hope was to use the PCIe 4.0 NVMe slot for faster storage and keep my boot drive on PCIe 3.0, but that didn't work out.

As for everything else, the board is great. More fan headers than you need. Probably enough USB for you unless you're a heavy user. The BIOS is a bit too user-friendly, with some power-user features hidden away in deep menus. My memory is a mix of two speeds, and it went for the higher speed settings. That didn't break anything, somehow, but I still manually lowered it for stability. It has enough SATA ports for most people, so you should be fine there. The integrated I/O shield is also nice, but a bit difficult to work with if your case is cramped with a motherboard of this size. My case can fit it, but the front drive cages mean that it takes some wiggling to get the motherboard past them.

2022年10月に購入、レビュー時点で3年と少しが経過していますが、元気に稼働中です。ものすごい耐久力と言っていいでしょう。
問題は何一つありません。BIOSアップデートにより、Ryzen 7 5800X3Dのカーブオプティマイザーを使っての動作すらできています（AMD公式には非対応とされています）。MSIのオーバークロックへの熱意は計り知れません。すごいです。
少し古い製品のため、PCIeスロットの固定方法は樹脂製（と思われる）のツメです。グラボを外す際など、力を込めすぎると外れたり折れたりします。注意が必要です。
バックプレートがマザーボードと一体化しており、組み立ての際にケースに差し込むだけで済むという素晴らしい作りになっています（カバーにいるドラゴンは、特に光ったりしません。商品写真だと目立っていますが、ケースの中では黒くて目立ちません）。
また、マザーボードのチップセットのヒートシンク付近にLEDがあり、「MSI center」というアプリで光り方をコントロールできます（私は使っておりませんが）。ちなみに、その付近にあるSATA端子ですが、横向き（右向き）です。HDDをたくさん使う方は、SATAケーブルの形や、ケース幅にも気を付けましょう。

総じてクオリティが高く、在庫さえあれば（昨今のメモリ高騰を考えてAM4で組む際も）今でも購入する価値のある素晴らしいマザーボードです。

timestamp_raw: Reviewed in Mexico on July 28, 2025

text:
Esse gabinete é um grande avanço comparado com o gabinete anterior que eu tinha e aqui destaco os 5 pontos positivos e 2 negativos:
1 - Primeiramente ele vem com uma porta USB-C 3.2, com transferência de até 20Gbps. É fato que o USB-C se popularizou, porém gabinetes que vem com conector USB-C com grandes taxas de transferência ainda são raros e os poucos gabinetes que vem tem uma porta USB-C 3.1, com velocidades de até 10Gbps.

2 - Os cabos do painel frontal são unificados, isso significa que não tem risco de conectar os cabos do HDD LED, POWER LED, POWER SW etc errados pois eles já vem em um único encaixe montado para ser conectado na placa mãe. Essa foi a maior vantagem que eu vi.

3 - Esse gabinete possui diversas aberturas para passagem de cabos. Entretanto, ao invés de aberturas de metal que contorcem (e às vezes até danifica), as aberturas desse gabinete da MSI utilizam uma espécie de plástico que "suaviza" essa passagem de cabos. De forma resumida, há menos riscos do cabo de alimentação da placa mãe ser contorcido desnecessariamente.

4 - Esse gabinete possui um controle RGB integrado. Basta conectar os cabos das ventoinhas RGB que ele gerencia as cores sozinho, sem precisar do software MSI Center instalado no PC.

5 - Esse gabinete vem com 4 ventoinhas RGB pré-instaladas, não sendo necessário comprar à parte.

6 - Esse gabinete vem com manual de instruções muito fraco. Uma pessoa leiga não irá saber montar corretamente, pois ele vem apenas com imagens ilustrativas. Não há passo a passo de montagem e tampouco o tipo de parafuso a ser utilizado.

7 - A tampa é de vidro temperado, que é consideravelmente mais pesada que o acrílico. Tem que tomar cuidado ao manusear a tampa do gabinete.

Uma dica importante: o cabo do controlador que vem na parte lateral direta deve ser conectado no conector JRAINBOW da placa-mãe, jamais conecte no conector SYSTEMFAN ou poderá queimar todas as ventoinhas

My MSI board is AM4 socket, and I find AMD's (old-school) sockets and processors easier to manipulate than Intel parts. CPU cooler attached solidly to board, and I have had no cooling issues with cpu. I found board layout to be logical and easy to work with. My only complaint is with the flimsy metallic I/O port cover for the back panel connectors, but then I have never seen one of these that actually fit the mainboard properly. Components I'm using with my B450 Tomahawk include: AMD Ryzen 5 3600 cpu w/Wraith Spire cooler, Corsair Vengence LPX DDR4 memory, EVGA GEForce GTX 960 graphics card, Western Digital 1TB and 2TB hdds, EVGA 750W G2 Supernova power supply and Antec Nine Hundred case (see picture of running system). The remainder of my experience with this mainboard will consist of long-term evaluation. So far, I can attest that the MSI B450 Tomahawk mainboard installs easily with the hardware detailed above and has run Linux 20.04 LTS for about 36 hours now without any issue. Still early, but happy so far.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
Although I didn't intend it this way, my first PC build turned into a build with several MSI parts, this motherboard included. The B450 Tomahawk is great value for the money. At the time that I bought this part, it was about $100 US. It came with some great features I utilize, and some great improvements versus the B350 version of this board.
1. The M.2 slot. This was moved to right below the CPU vs on the B350 board it was below the graphics card. This improves with the thermals of anything you have installed in the M.2 slot. It is a great addition to the board and I use it with my NVMe drive. While it does eliminate the usage of the SATA 5 and 6 ports. You still have 4 others to use. To be honest, if you are installing more than for drives into your system, you need to be buying larger drives rather than more.
2. The RGB headers are a great addition. I use them for my Deepcool RF 140 front fans. They are paired with Mystic Light from MSI, so they match the breathing pattern of the under glow lights off to the right on the motherboard. Speaking of which, those lights underneath that one side are much brighter than I thought. Not too bright, but bright enough that they are noticeable. I was afraid they would be hidden by the case, but they show up perfectly.
3. The different headers on the back are amazing. I love that they have USB 3.1 Gen 2 and Gen 1 ports on the back. I currently have my keyboard and mouse in the Gen 1 ports. The Gen 2 ports (one is a USB-C and one is USB-A) are saved for other items. For example, one will be for an external hard drive/backup drive that I will be purchasing in a short time.
4. I find the BIOS/UEFI easy to understand. For context, the beginner mode is great for those starting out. And if the advanced mode is great for more experienced people. Even though I'm a beginner, I had an easy time understanding a good amount of what was in the advanced mode. I of course had to look things up on Google/YouTube and in the manual, but I still was able to navigate and understand it. I also loved that I could use a mouse in the BIOS. Made it easier than having to use the keyboard to click through options. I also found it helpful that they explained what certain things did within the BIOS. They had a help section, which is AWESOME for beginners that need help with adjusting any setting in there.
If there's one thing I could go back and do, I think I might have gone with the MSI B450 Pro Carbon AC simply because it would free up a PCIe slot for me. I'm using a WIFI card and the Pro Carbon has Wifi built in. I know most people will be using Ethernet for a desktop, and if I were using Ethernet to connect my PC to the web, I would use the B450 Tomahawk over the Pro Carbon.
Overall, well worth the price and great for building a PC on a budget if you don't need all the extra features of the X470 boards.

The Bios flash is easy to do with the firmware file loaded onto a USB key. (I didn't try the funky flash button, did it from the interface.) I wish MSI provided a Windows app to download and update the Bios, as some other brands do, but this is a minor thing.

For the price paid, the value of this mobo is excellent. I highly recommend considering it for a mid-priced Ryzen build.

text:

A really good value board in the world of today. If you want to start with a "budget" system and upgrade as time goes on, this is a WONDERFUL board for that. Started with an i5-12600KF and plan on upgrading to 14th gen Intel when prices cool off. It's pretty easy to install, everything came as advertised, and there were no issues or unexpected things, at least to the eye of a new PC builder in summer '25. Seems barebones, but comes with some neat features, especially in regard to the onboard sound, M.2 heatsink, and reinforced PCIe x16 slot. Like seriously, maybe it's just me, but the back audio jack for the on-board sound (the green one) sounds like... really good. MSI BIOS also seems pretty stable in regard to RAM overclocking, but maybe that's more software design, who knows...

Pros:
- Four DIMM slots for RAM. Hey, to me, I thought this was neat. Guess with DDR5 motherboards two slots is more common (?) but DDR4 seems to have all 4 DIMMs available.
- A heatsink for one of your M.2 drives. Didn't expect a board of this spec to come with one. Great for PCIe Gen 4 speed drives that get really hot (I'm looking at you, Sabrent...).
- Surprisingly good onboard sound... Like, super surprised. You won't need any PCIe SoundBlaster card or anything if you just use the back jack, the sound "core" or whatever they call it on the board seems to have some kick to it!
- USB 3 support. Not a super big thing in modern day, but to me it was sweet. Good stuff!

Neutral:
- PCIe Gen 4 speeds. Not really an issue, given most hardware won't really even take advantage of PCIe gen 5 speeds nowadays, but if you have a 5070 Ti or higher and really want to get your money's worth, keep this in mind.

Cons:
- Lack of screw specification. For the smaller screws, they look REALLY similar. If you're not careful and use the ones with the slightly taller heads, you"ll cross-thread it in and get em stuck. Glad about the upgrade potential cause that motherboard is like permanently part of the case now, lol...

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
Running very cool temps and I do believe this board to be a big part of that. It seems to disperse heat very well. Gaming with a 9700X on 105w mode I have not seen my CPU temp go over 62°C. Using a cheap 6 heat pipe horizontally mounted radiator CPU cooler with 120mm Noctua.
It's been plug and play, every easy to flash but find the YouTube videos that discuss proper USB formatted drives, notably FAT32 with MBH partitions. You MUST have another working computer to flash the BIOS prior to first system boot if building new using a 9000 series AMD CPU.

BIOS is extremely easy to use and with F7 will switch between easy mode or advanced mode. One click overclocking for CPU and RAM, AMD SAM was already enabled and ready to go. No bloatware except a single bottom corner Norton security pop up when powering on the system each time but I believe that is from MSI Afterburner software if you refuse it when downloading. Otherwise just don't get MSI Afterburner and you won't get the pop up. Norton security is nowhere else to be found thankfully.

WIFI does not work when first time booting, must use Ethernet cable, and download wifi driver later. Of which the antenna works really well and 16 feet from my router through two walls I am only seeing a 60mbs drop in speed, getting 240 out of 300mb/s.

This thing is quite large so do be sure to check your case dimensions.

Comes with NVME thermal plates with built in pads on top and bottom of NVME and the bottom plate cannot be removed so third party NVME heat sink cannot be used. But with this built in top and bottom I don't see the need for additional cooling as what's there seems to be sufficient. However if you get a thicker NVME with a built in heatsink/graphene strip, at just 4mm it's nearly too thick to mount it between both thermal pads with heat sink plates. They really need to fix this on this board but not a deal breaker....unless you got a thick NVME of course like a SAMSUNG EVO or BLACK. My HP 4TB NVME has a graphene thermal tape strip on it and it was difficult to sandwich in there.

Overall highly pleased, board is overbuilt making it solid, cool running, and you don't have to worry about pulling too much power or power limitations.

DELL XPS 8700 Windows 8.1 this card works just fine for dual monitors. But you will need to go into BIOS and disable secure boot mode. I used the onboard graphics while setting this up. I used the HDMI plug (it has a cap hiding it, just pull the cap out and plug in your HDMI TV or monitor). Take your graphics card OUT when doing this. Restart you your computer and Hit F2 when you see the Dell splash screen. Now arrow over to BIOS and change the setting to disable secure boot mode. Exit and restart your computer. Now shut down the computer and put in the new graphics card hook up the HDMI TV and monitor and restart. You should now be good to go.

BLACK screens and 5 Beeps!
I started out assuming I could just plug and play. But I ended up with black screens and was getting 5 beeps. People kept saying the 5 beeps meant the battery on the mother board was bad or needed to be reseated. That is if you get 5 beeps over and over not 5 beeps and then stops. Luckily I could put my old card back in to do the research. I did not realize there was an onboard HDMI hook up on my DELL until I kept exchanging the cards in and out. I had a hard time getting rid of the drivers I loaded from the start, I used the CD that came with the card. But with the drivers loaded the method above would not work.
